issues.suggestion: I carry my bag in front of me so my wallet won't be snatched on dark streets at night.

issues.concern: 引っ手繰る is the kanji spelling of ひったくる itself, not a separate word that ひったくる intensifies.
issues.suggestion: ひったくる can be written 引っ手繰る and is formed from 手繰る with the intensifying prefix 引っ-.

issues.concern: The explanation gives kabosu the size typically associated with sudachi. Kabosu are generally closer to tennis-ball size, not golf-ball size.
issues.suggestion: Replace "about the size of a golf ball" with "about the size of a tennis ball".

issues.concern: 乗る does not exclude the driver or operator; it can describe riding a bicycle or being in a car as its driver.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "乗る — to ride; to get on or into (does not specify whether one is the driver or a passenger)".

issues.concern: The etymological breakdown incorrectly identifies さる as the first component. さりげない derives from さりげ（然り気, 'such an appearance') + ない, with さり rather than さる.
issues.suggestion: Replace the breakdown with: "さりげない consists of さりげ（然り気, 'such an appearance') + ない, conveying the absence of any outward sign of a particular intention."

issues.concern: The sentence incorrectly describes a change from 雨 to the identical character 雨. In 雨粒, it is the reading that changes, not the kanji.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "In 雨粒, 雨 is read あま rather than あめ."

issues.concern: っ人 is not a suffix meaning 'person'; 助っ人 is a sound-changed form of 助人（すけびと）.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "助っ人 developed through sound change from 助人（すけびと）, meaning a person who helps."

issues.concern: The sentence incorrectly describes a change in the kanji; the change here is in its reading, from ふね to ふな.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "In 船便, 船 is read ふな rather than its standalone reading ふね."

issues.concern: "Drew back my childhood memories" is not an idiomatic English expression for recalling memories.
issues.suggestion: Looking at old photos, I recalled my childhood memories one by one.

issues.concern: The description incorrectly makes a sink a defining component of ユニットバス. A prefabricated bathing room can be a ユニットバス without a sink or toilet.
issues.suggestion: ユニットバス is a prefabricated bathing-room module; some configurations also include a sink and toilet.

issues.concern: 現役 does not mean someone who passes on their first attempt. In this context, it refers to taking entrance exams while still in school, regardless of the result.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 現役: a student taking entrance exams while still in school, without an intervening 浪人 year.

issues.concern: お小遣い need not be regular or unrelated to a task; it can also be occasional spending money, including money given for helping with an errand.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 「お小遣い: allowance, pocket money — money for personal spending」.

issues.concern: 鍋蓋 denotes a pot lid or a kanji radical, not food.
issues.suggestion: Remove the "food" tag.

issues.concern: The claim that わだかまり is always written in hiragana is false: it can also be written 蟠り, as the entry itself notes.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "The word is usually written in hiragana."

issues.concern: 有望 is also commonly used predicatively, especially in 将来有望だ; it is not almost always a modifier before a noun.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Used both before nouns (有望な人材) and predicatively (将来有望だ)."

issues.concern: “Flammables strictly prohibited” incorrectly prohibits flammable materials. 火気厳禁 prohibits flames and other ignition sources, often precisely because flammable materials are present.
issues.suggestion: Replace with “no open flames; ignition sources strictly prohibited”.

issues.concern: “Flammables strictly prohibited” incorrectly prohibits flammable materials rather than flames and other ignition sources.
issues.suggestion: Replace with “no open flames; ignition sources strictly prohibited”.

issues.concern: スイッチ is a general term for a switch, not specifically a toggle or flip-type control; push-button switches are also スイッチ.
issues.suggestion: Change to: スイッチ: switch — a general term covering push-button, toggle, and other switch types.

issues.concern: The explanation incorrectly makes the absence of falling snow a requirement. 地吹雪 refers to wind lifting accumulated snow and can occur whether or not snow is also falling.
issues.suggestion: Replace the final sentence with: "It involves existing snow being swept up by wind and can occur even when no new snow is falling."

issues.concern: This conflates traditional Japanese 群青 pigment with lapis-lazuli ultramarine. Traditional 群青 used in Japanese painting was made from azurite (藍銅鉱), not lapis lazuli.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Traditional Japanese 群青 pigment was made from azurite (藍銅鉱)." Correct the same lapis-lazuli origin claim in the definition's explanation.

issues.concern: Japan has no legal requirement that smartphone cameras make an unsilenceable shutter sound; this is an industry practice, not a legal mandate.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Smartphones sold for the Japanese market commonly have a shutter sound that cannot normally be silenced, an industry practice intended partly to deter secret photography."

issues.concern: The neutral formality label contradicts the notes' explicit description of the word as formal.
issues.suggestion: Change formality to "formal".

issues.concern: 落札 means winning a bid, not the successful bidder. The person or company is 落札者.
issues.suggestion: Change to "- 落札: winning a bid" or "- 落札: winning a bid; 落札者: the successful bidder".

issues.concern: 入場券 means an admission ticket, which may be paid or free; payment is not part of its meaning.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "- 入場券: admission ticket — a ticket for entry".

issues.concern: Colloquial がっぽり can be used in polite speech with です／ます; its informal register does not prohibit polite sentence endings.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Generally avoided in formal writing, but can be used in conversational polite speech."

issues.concern: The established expression is 旧交を温める, not 旧知を温める. The entry presents a mistaken substitution as a common collocation.
issues.suggestion: Replace this item with 「旧交を温める: to renew an old friendship」 and clarify that it uses 旧交, a different word.

issues.concern: 万物生きとし生けるもの is not an established collocation. It conflates 万物, which includes inanimate things, with 生きとし生けるもの, meaning all living things.
issues.suggestion: Remove this collocation, or list 生きとし生けるもの separately as a related expression meaning “all living things.”

issues.concern: The claimed kabuki origin is incorrect. 定番 is not derived from a theatrical term for a fixed program or repertoire.
issues.suggestion: Delete the sentence claiming a kabuki origin.

issues.concern: 支那そば remains an established name for ramen, including in restaurant names, and is not generally treated as offensive. The note incorrectly transfers the sensitivity surrounding 支那 as a name for China to the dish name as a whole.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 支那そば: an older name for ramen, still used by some restaurants.

issues.concern: The explanation incorrectly excludes head hair and facial hair. 体毛 can include all hair covering the body, including those types.
issues.suggestion: Replace the explanation with: "Hair growing on the body. Often used for arm hair, leg hair, chest hair, etc., but can also include head and facial hair."

issues.concern: The attachment rule is incorrect: 最中に does not normally follow a verb's dictionary form + の. The verb examples correctly use the ている form directly before 最中に.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Attaches to noun + の or verb ている form: 食事の最中に／話している最中に."

issues.concern: 'If anything' means 'if at all' or 'on the contrary'; it does not convey the decisive alternative expressed by いっそのこと.
issues.suggestion: Remove 'if anything' from both the main gloss and definitions[0].gloss; retain 'might as well; rather'.

issues.concern: The translation omits を超える: the amount ingested exceeded the lethal dose, rather than merely being a lethal dose.
issues.suggestion: An amount of the drug exceeding the lethal dose was ingested.

issues.concern: The quotation is from the end of section 52 of 徒然草, not its opening.
issues.suggestion: Replace "The famous opening of 徒然草" with "The famous conclusion of section 52 of 徒然草".

issues.concern: "Mixed feelings" means conflicting emotions, whereas 半信半疑 refers to uncertainty about whether something is true.
issues.suggestion: Replace "to take something with mixed feelings" with "to receive something with skepticism."

issues.concern: The き in 能書き is not a suffix added to 能書; it is the okurigana of 書き, the noun form of 書く.
issues.suggestion: Remove the suffix analysis. Explain that 書き means 'writing' and that the word originally referred to a written description of a medicine's efficacy.

issues.concern: 募金する can also mean donating money in response to a fundraising appeal, so explicitly saying it does not mean giving is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 「募金する: to collect donations; also, to donate money in response to a fundraising appeal」.

issues.concern: The pronunciation note gives the headword's kanji instead of an alternate reading.
issues.suggestion: Replace 「Also read as 施術」 with 「Also read as しじゅつ」.

issues.concern: "Plastic bags became paid" is not idiomatic English for bags no longer being free and could teach an incorrect expression.
issues.suggestion: Since the supermarket started charging for plastic bags, I carry a reusable shopping bag with me.

issues.concern: Standalone 在日 conventionally refers to Zainichi Koreans, not to Chinese residents as a parallel established usage.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "As a standalone noun, it often refers specifically to ethnic Koreans (在日韓国・朝鮮人) living in Japan."

issues.concern: The official police report is called 遺失届 (or 遺失届出書). 紛失届 is a commonly understood alternative, not the official police term.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "紛失届 is commonly used for a report of a lost item; the official police term is 遺失届 (遺失届出書)."

issues.concern: "Checked baggage is often paid" is not natural English for baggage that incurs a fee. 有料 means passengers must pay for the service.
issues.suggestion: Since budget airlines often charge for checked baggage, I try to manage with just carry-on.

issues.concern: 物腰 does not literally mean 'the way one carries things'; this gives a false account of the word's meaning and formation.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "物腰 refers to a person's bearing, demeanor, or manner of interacting with others."

issues.concern: The notes explicitly describe the term as formal, contradicting the neutral formality label.
issues.suggestion: Revise the note to describe 清掃員 as a standard occupational title without labeling it formal.

issues.concern: 血まみれ and 汗まみれ use the ～まみれ pattern, not ～浸し, so they are not examples of the stated pattern.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Related expressions include 血まみれ (covered in blood) and 汗まみれ (covered in sweat), which use the separate ～まみれ pattern."

issues.concern: The Japanese incorrectly uses intransitive くじける with the object 足首を. The English corresponds to transitive くじく.
issues.suggestion: Change the Japanese to 「足首がくじけた。」 to illustrate the headword, or 「足首をくじいた。」 to match the transitive English.

issues.concern: The Japanese incorrectly uses intransitive くじける with 足を. 'I twisted my foot' corresponds to 足をくじいた.
issues.suggestion: Change the Japanese to 「階段で足がくじけた。」 to retain the headword.

issues.concern: The Japanese incorrectly uses intransitive くじける with 足を; the English renders the intended transitive expression 足をくじく.
issues.suggestion: Change the Japanese to 「走っている途中で足がくじけて、試合を棄権した。」 to retain the headword.

issues.concern: 書き写す does not require copying a text in full; it can also describe copying selected portions. The same incorrect restriction appears earlier in the notes.
issues.suggestion: Describe 書き写す as copying or transcribing text, without inherently emphasizing selection, whereas 書き抜く specifically emphasizes selecting portions to copy.

issues.concern: 天使 did not originate in a Christian context. It was used before Christianity reached Japan for a heavenly or imperial messenger.
issues.suggestion: Replace the opening clause with: "While its angel sense is associated especially with Christianity,".

issues.concern: Japanese road rules do not generally prohibit crossing all solid lines. A solid white lane divider permits lane changes; restrictions depend on the marking's color and function.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "On Japanese roads, the meaning depends on the line's color and function: solid white lane dividers permit lane changes, while solid yellow lane dividers prohibit them."

issues.concern: 二点鎖線 is not the standard line type for centerlines. Centerlines conventionally use 一点鎖線; 二点鎖線 is used for phantom outlines, such as alternate positions of moving parts.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 「二点鎖線 — double-dot-dash line; used for phantom outlines, such as alternate positions of moving parts」.

issues.concern: The explanation says there are typically two braids on each side, implying four braids. The typical hairstyle has two braids total, one on each side.
issues.suggestion: Change "typically in two braids on each side of the head" to "typically in two braids, one on each side of the head".

issues.concern: The 当用漢字 list was replaced by the 常用漢字 list in 1981, not 2010.
路線バス means a bus operating on a fixed route, not specifically within a city. Routes may cross municipal boundaries or serve rural areas; 高速バス can also be 路線バス.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 「路線バス: scheduled route bus — operates on a fixed route」.

issues.concern: The spouse is not first in a succession hierarchy ahead of children. A surviving spouse inherits alongside the highest-priority eligible blood relatives.
issues.suggestion: State that a surviving spouse is always a legal heir; among blood relatives, descendants have priority, followed by lineal ascendants, then siblings.

issues.concern: Kimono are not necessarily sewn entirely by hand; machine-sewn and partly machine-sewn kimono also exist.
issues.suggestion: Replace “kimono are sewn entirely by hand” with “kimono are traditionally sewn by hand”.

issues.concern: "The new song recorded a major hit" is not idiomatic English for a song achieving commercial success.
issues.suggestion: The new song became a major hit.

issues.concern: ベストセラー is not restricted to books; it also describes other high-selling products.
issues.suggestion: Replace "specifically for books" with "often used for books, but also for other products".

issues.concern: The wrapping direction is reversed: 衣に青じそを巻く means wrapping green shiso around the batter, not wrapping the shiso in batter.
issues.suggestion: For the intended English meaning, change the Japanese to 「青じそに天ぷらの衣をつけて揚げると、香りが良くて食欲をそそる。」

issues.concern: 絡む is a separate verb, not an alternative dictionary form of 絡まる. The pestering examples use 絡まれる, the passive of 絡む, not of the headword 絡まる.
issues.suggestion: Clarify: 「For pestering, the related verb 絡む is normally used. Its passive is 絡まれる; the passive of 絡まる would be 絡まられる.」

issues.concern: The English adds the purpose of avoiding a crowd, which is not stated in the Japanese.
issues.suggestion: Let's go at a different time.

issues.concern: 「私腹を貪る」 conflates 「私腹を肥やす」 (to line one's own pockets) with expressions such as 「暴利を貪る」 (to seek excessive profits). It is not the standard idiom for the stated meaning.
issues.suggestion: Replace this collocation with 「暴利を貪る: to seek excessive profits」 and revise example 5 to use 「私腹を肥やす」 rather than 「私腹を貪る」.

issues.concern: 罵る does not imply sustained abuse rather than a single remark; it can describe a single abusive utterance, such as calling someone 「ばか」.
issues.suggestion: Remove this sentence or replace it with: "Can describe either a single abusive remark or repeated verbal abuse."

issues.concern: ごとく is not a classical Japanese particle; it is the continuative (連用形) form of the classical auxiliary ごとし.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "The continuative form of the classical auxiliary ごとし, meaning 'like' or 'as.'"

issues.concern: 通過 can also describe substances passing through materials, as in 水がフィルターを通過する; it is not restricted to people or vehicles.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 通過: passing through — a general term for passage through a place or object; unlike 透過, it does not specifically emphasize transmission through a material.

issues.concern: Tsugaru shamisen plectrums are not generally larger and heavier than those used in other styles; they are typically relatively small, especially compared with gidayū plectrums.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "The 撥 used in 津軽三味線 is typically relatively small, with a thick handle and a narrow striking edge."

issues.concern: 公然 is a ト・タル adjective, not a regular な-adjective; 公然な is not its standard attributive form.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Used adverbially as 公然と and attributively as 公然たる or 公然の."

issues.concern: 取扱店 means a store that carries or sells a particular product; it does not imply authorization or a license to sell.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 取扱店: stockist; retailer carrying a particular product".

issues.concern: 美容整形 names a surgical procedure, not a body part.
issues.suggestion: Remove the "body-part" tag; retain "health".

issues.concern: 煮豆 is not specifically savory; it includes sweet simmered beans, such as sweetened black soybeans.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 煮豆: simmered beans — often seasoned with sugar and soy sauce".

issues.concern: "Rest area" normally means a roadside stopping facility or a designated space for taking a break, not a destination for recuperation such as 保養地.
issues.suggestion: Remove "rest area"; retain "health resort; retreat; convalescence destination".

issues.concern: 普通車 means an ordinary-class train car, not specifically a non-reserved car. Ordinary-class cars can have reserved or non-reserved seating, so contrasting 普通車 with 指定席車 is incorrect. The main gloss repeats this error.
issues.suggestion: Remove 'non-reserved' from the main gloss and this sense's gloss. Revise the explanation to: 'An ordinary-class train car, as opposed to a Green Car. Seating may be reserved or non-reserved.'

issues.concern: The seasoning's name is misspelled: fermented black beans are 豆豉, not 豆鼓.
issues.suggestion: Replace 豆鼓醤 with 豆豉醤.

issues.concern: 国番号 is a country calling code (such as 81 for Japan), not an international dialing prefix (such as 00 or 011).
issues.suggestion: Change to: '- 国番号: country calling code — identifies the destination country in an international telephone number'.

issues.concern: 熱さ means hotness or intensity, not a medical fever. Fever is 熱 or 発熱.
issues.suggestion: Remove "fever": "heat; hotness; fervor".

issues.concern: 名言 emphasizes the excellence or insightfulness of the words, not their fame or the speaker's fame.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 名言: memorable or insightful saying — emphasizes how well the words express an important truth"

issues.concern: 住人 does not imply or emphasize long-term residence; it can also refer to someone who has just moved in.
issues.suggestion: Replace “emphasizes being a longtime inhabitant” with “refers to someone living in a particular dwelling or place.”

issues.concern: This incorrectly states that all legal name changes require family court approval. Surname changes resulting from marriage or divorce generally do not.
issues.suggestion: Qualify the claim: changing a given name, or changing a surname outside procedures such as marriage or divorce, generally requires family court permission and legally sufficient reasons.

issues.concern: The Japanese states that the speaker attended the party at a friend's invitation; the English states only that the speaker was invited.
issues.suggestion: I attended a singles party at a friend's invitation.

issues.concern: 主に is an adverb meaning 'mainly', not an adjective or a predicate form of 主な. The sentence incorrectly presents an adverbial form as suitable for predicate use.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "The related adverb 主に means 'mainly'."

issues.concern: 発車する is not restricted to trains and buses or to departures from stations; it also describes cars and other land vehicles starting to move.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 「発車する: to depart; to start moving — used for land vehicles such as trains, buses, and cars」.

issues.concern: 通過する can also describe light or radiation passing through a space or material; the categorical exclusion is false.
issues.suggestion: Replace “not for light or radiation” with “透過する specifically emphasizes transmission through a material.”

issues.concern: 筋違い does not name a body part. Its physical sense denotes a muscle strain or crick.
issues.suggestion: Remove the "body-part" tag.

issues.concern: "Port of call" denotes the port visited (寄港地), not the act of stopping there (寄港).
issues.suggestion: Change to "calling at a port; making a port call".

issues.concern: 寄港 can also describe an aircraft stopping at an intermediate airport, so the categorical exclusion of aircraft is false.
issues.suggestion: Replace the opening restriction with: "Used for ships stopping at ports, and also for aircraft stopping at intermediate airports."

issues.concern: 入港 means entering a port; it does not imply that the port is the final destination.
issues.suggestion: Change to "- 入港: entering a port".

issues.concern: 几帳面 is not derived from 帳面 or from neat pleats. It originally referred to the carefully finished, chamfered edges of the supporting posts of a 几帳, a curtained partition rather than a folding screen.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 「几帳面: meticulous, methodical, precise — originally a term for the chamfered edges of the supporting posts of a 几帳 (curtained partition), not a derivative of 帳面.」

issues.concern: 見違える also means to mistake one person or thing for another. The categorical claim that it is not about making mistakes is false.
issues.suggestion: Explain that 見違える can also mean visual misidentification, but is commonly used for a change so dramatic that someone or something is hardly recognizable. Remove the categorical contrast in WATCH OUT as well.

issues.concern: "Say such easygoing things" is not idiomatic English and obscures the criticism that the speaker is treating an urgent situation too casually.
issues.suggestion: Don't talk as if there's no hurry.

issues.concern: "Say leisurely things" is an unnatural calque. Here 悠長なこと refers to remarks that treat the situation as less urgent than it is.
issues.suggestion: In an emergency like this, we can't afford to talk as if there's no rush.

issues.concern: “Between non-regular employees” specifies disparities within that group. The Japanese does not specify the comparison group and ordinarily refers to unequal treatment relative to regular employees.
issues.suggestion: Disparities in the treatment of non-regular employees are becoming an issue.

issues.concern: The expression is not restricted to this pattern. It can modify a noun with 明らかな, and the preceding topic need not be a clause.
issues.suggestion: Replace “Always used” with “Often used” and remove the restriction that the preceding material must be a clause.

issues.concern: 荒涼 is a タリ adjective; 荒涼な is not its standard attributive form, rather than merely a less common one.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Use 荒涼たる or 荒涼とした before a noun, not 荒涼な in standard Japanese."

issues.concern: 相当額 means an equivalent or corresponding amount, not a considerable amount. The latter is expressed by 相当な額.
issues.suggestion: Change to 「相当額: an equivalent amount」.

issues.concern: 被曝 does not mean exposure is involuntary; it also includes intentional medical exposure, such as diagnostic imaging.
issues.suggestion: Remove “(involuntary)” and describe 被曝 as exposure to radiation.

issues.concern: 店 in 花屋の店 is an independent noun modified by 花屋の, not a suffix.
issues.suggestion: Replace the suffix example with 新宿店 and clarify that 店 as a suffix is read てん.

issues.concern: 圏 is read けん in 語圏 as well; かん is not an alternative reading used here.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "圏 is read けん in these compounds."

issues.concern: This confuses numbered memorial observances (回忌) with elapsed anniversaries. 三回忌, 七回忌, and 十三回忌 occur on the second, sixth, and twelfth death anniversaries, respectively.
issues.suggestion: Change the intervals to 'the first, second, sixth, and twelfth anniversaries (一周忌, 三回忌, 七回忌, and 十三回忌).'

issues.concern: The translation omits 歴史 in 歴史小説, losing the specification that it is a historical novel.
issues.suggestion: The historical novel depicts a protagonist who plays an active role as a spy.

issues.concern: 翌月 is not restricted to a referenced past event; it can also refer to the month after a future date or event.
issues.suggestion: Replace "a referenced past event" with "a referenced date or event, whether past or future".

issues.concern: "We blossomed into nostalgic conversation" is not idiomatic English. 話に花が咲いた means that the conversation became lively, not that the speakers blossomed into conversation.
issues.suggestion: I reunited with old friends at a class reunion, and we had a lively conversation reminiscing about old times.

issues.concern: "I enjoyed it more than enough" is unnatural English for thorough enjoyment and can suggest an unwanted excess. 十二分に楽しめた expresses having enjoyed something fully.
issues.suggestion: I thoroughly enjoyed it.

issues.concern: 木枯らし does not specifically mean the first cold wind of the season; that distinction belongs to 木枯らし一号.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "木枯らし: cold wintry wind — a strong, cold wind in late autumn or early winter".

issues.concern: Having no moves available does not necessarily mean losing, particularly in go, where players may pass and the winner is determined by scoring.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "The expression figuratively describes having no effective move or measure left."

issues.concern: Informal vocabulary can occur in polite speech; いちゃもん is not excluded from sentences using polite forms.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Generally avoided in formal contexts, but can occur in otherwise polite speech."

issues.concern: This incorrectly attributes the origin of 詭弁 to ancient Greek philosophy. 詭弁 is a Sino-Japanese term with antecedents in Chinese; the Greek connection concerns the English word “sophistry.”
issues.suggestion: Replace with: “The English equivalent ‘sophistry’ is associated with the Sophists of ancient Greece.”

issues.concern: 洗面 means washing one's face; it is not a broader term that also denotes hand washing.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 「洗面: washing one's face; often used in the compound 洗面所 (washroom)」.

issues.concern: 毅然 is a と・たる adjective (形容動詞), not a noun.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "The adverbial と form of 毅然, a と・たる adjective."

issues.concern: 平然 is not a na-adjective: it does not normally modify nouns with な. 平然とした顔 illustrates modification with とした, not na-adjective usage.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Modifies nouns with とした (平然とした顔) or, more formally, たる (平然たる態度), and is used adverbially with と (平然と)."

issues.concern: The change from ふく to ぷく is 半濁音化 (a change to a p-sound), not rendaku.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Note the sound change: 服 (ふく) becomes ぷく after 軍 (ぐん), giving ぐんぷく."

issues.concern: 出入口 is also used for vehicle entrances and exits; it is not restricted to buildings.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 出入口: entrance/exit — a general term used for buildings, vehicles, and other spaces.

issues.concern: 断層 means a geological fault, not a stratum. A geological stratum is 地層.
issues.suggestion: Change the line to "- 断層: geological fault".

issues.concern: 駆除する is also commonly used for removing computer viruses and malware, so its use is not restricted to living things.
issues.suggestion: State that it is generally used for eliminating pests and other unwanted organisms, but also for removing computer viruses and malware.

issues.concern: 離婚慰謝料 is compensation for emotional distress associated with divorce, not alimony (financial support paid to a former spouse).
issues.suggestion: Replace "divorce alimony/consolation money" with "compensation for emotional distress related to divorce".

issues.concern: 考えが甘さだ incorrectly uses the noun 甘さ as though it were the adjective 甘い; it does not express the English meaning.
issues.suggestion: Change the Japanese to 「考えの甘さを指摘された。」 to retain the headword and match the English.

issues.concern: Shingon uses the reading わじょう, not かしょう.
issues.suggestion: Change the sect assignments to かしょう (Tendai) and わじょう (Shingon and some other sects).

issues.concern: 温泉卵 typically has a softly set, custard-like yolk and a looser white, not a set white and runny yolk.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 温泉卵: hot spring egg — gently cooked egg with a softly set yolk and a loose, barely set white.

issues.concern: "Rescued by a narrow escape from death" incorrectly makes the escape the means of rescue and is unnatural English.
issues.suggestion: The building collapsed in the major earthquake, but I was rescued, narrowly escaping death.

issues.concern: 砂糖漬け does not exclude cooking; it includes foods cooked in sugar syrup, such as candied citrus peel.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 砂糖漬け: food preserved in sugar or sugar syrup".

issues.concern: Skewer grilling is not the opposite of whole roasting: whole fish or animals can be roasted on skewers or spits.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "- 串焼き: skewer grilling — food grilled on skewers".

issues.concern: "To pursue responsibility" is not an idiomatic English expression for demanding accountability and can suggest seeking responsibility instead.
issues.suggestion: Translate as "To hold someone accountable."

issues.concern: 出力されない is passive, making the printer the thing being output. The English instead describes the printer failing to output correctly.
issues.suggestion: Change the Japanese to 「プリンターが正しく出力しないので、ドライバーを再インストールした。」 to match the English.

issues.concern: This confuses 速める with 早める. 速める means to increase speed or pace; making something happen sooner is typically 早める.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 速める: to speed up — emphasizes increasing speed or pace".

issues.concern: 数十億 means several billion, not tens of billions. 億 is one hundred million.
issues.suggestion: Change to "数十億: several billion".

issues.concern: “Moral behavior ... has become a problem” suggests that behaving ethically is itself problematic. The Japanese says that ethical standards or conduct on social media have become an issue.
issues.suggestion: Ethical standards on social media have become a concern.

issues.concern: 道徳 is a Sino-Japanese word, not a native Japanese (和語) word.
issues.suggestion: Replace “the native Japanese word” with “a Sino-Japanese word.”

issues.concern: The etymology incorrectly derives the expression from serving food on a large tray. 大盤 is an ateji spelling, not the source of the expression.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Derived from 椀飯振る舞い (おうばんぶるまい), referring to lavishly entertaining guests with food. The pronunciation later changed to おおばんぶるまい, with 大盤 used as an ateji spelling."

issues.concern: 不自然 alone is not the adverbial form; adverbial use requires に.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "不自然: the base form without な; used adverbially as 不自然に."

issues.concern: 組織 can also denote the act of organizing, as in 組織する; it is not restricted to the resulting structured body.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 組織: organization — can refer to an organized body or the act of organizing; 組織化 explicitly emphasizes the process."

issues.concern: 勾留 is not limited to detention during investigation or before trial; it also applies to defendants during trial.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 勾留: detention of a suspect or defendant in criminal proceedings — same reading but different kanji; distinct from 拘留 as a criminal penalty".

issues.concern: 留置 does not specifically mean detention at a police station. It can refer to holding someone in custody in other facilities as well.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 留置: holding in custody, including detention at a police station".

issues.concern: 息を止める describes holding one's breath, an action, not a body part.
issues.suggestion: Remove the semantic tag "body-part".

issues.concern: 不時着 does not necessarily involve a crash landing; an emergency landing may be completed safely without damage.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "不時着する: to make an emergency landing — to land somewhere other than the intended destination because of an emergency."

issues.concern: 盗み聞き means deliberately listening secretly, not accidentally overhearing. Here, 〜てしまった can express regret without making the listening accidental.
issues.suggestion: Translate as: "I ended up eavesdropping on the conversation in the next room."

issues.concern: Neither 図々しい nor 嫌らしい contains the suffix ～たらしい.
issues.suggestion: Delete this sentence, or use genuine examples of ～たらしい such as 未練たらしい and 貧乏たらしい.

issues.concern: ため息をつく means to sigh; it does not name a body part.
issues.suggestion: Remove the "body-part" tag.

issues.concern: 強行敢行 is not an established Japanese compound or common collocation meaning "forced execution." It incorrectly combines two separate words.
issues.suggestion: Remove this collocation.

issues.concern: 水を振りかける is a literal use meaning to sprinkle water, not a figurative use.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Can also be used with liquids, e.g., 水を振りかける (to sprinkle water)."

issues.concern: かける is commonly used for dry ingredients too, as in 塩をかける and 砂糖をかける. The stated contrast is misleading.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- かける: to put or pour over; broader than 振りかける and used for both liquids and dry ingredients"

issues.concern: あっぱれ derives from あはれ (modern あわれ), not from words meaning a clear sky. 天晴 is an ateji spelling, so the proposed sky metaphor is not its etymology.
issues.suggestion: Replace the etymology with: "Derived from あはれ (modern あわれ) through consonant gemination. 天晴 is an ateji spelling." Also correct the earlier claim that it is originally from 天晴.

issues.concern: 名店街 is a shopping area or arcade containing well-known shops or restaurants, not specifically a famous restaurant district.
issues.suggestion: Change the gloss to "shopping area of well-known shops and restaurants".

issues.concern: お足を運びください misforms the honorific request: the お in the お＋verb stem＋ください construction belongs before 運び, not before 足.
issues.suggestion: Replace お足を運びください with 足をお運びください.

issues.concern: The literal explanation reverses the meaning: the expression means that stopping or avoiding something is not possible, not that one has no choice but to stop.
issues.suggestion: Replace "cannot do other than stop" with "cannot stop or avoid it".

issues.concern: "To be a handful" reverses the roles: it describes the troublesome person or thing, whereas 手を焼く describes the person having difficulty handling them. This also occurs in definitions[0].gloss.
issues.suggestion: Replace "to be a handful" with "to have one's hands full" in both glosses.

issues.concern: The absolute claim that 〜てあげる is never used for the speaker is false. It can express doing something for oneself, as in 自分を褒めてあげる.
issues.suggestion: Replace “never for the speaker” with “usually for someone other than the speaker; it can also be used for oneself, as in 自分を褒めてあげる.”

issues.concern: The touchscreen action タップ does not denote a leisure activity; the "leisure" tag assigns an unrelated domain.
issues.suggestion: Remove "leisure" from the semantic tags.

issues.concern: スワイプ also describes gestures on trackpads, so it is not exclusive to touchscreens.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Used for sliding gestures on touchscreens and trackpads."

issues.concern: ボタン was borrowed from Portuguese botão, not English.
issues.suggestion: Change “button, from English” to “button, from Portuguese”.

issues.concern: The standard collocations for turning power on and off are 電源を入れる and 電源を切る, not 電源ボタンを入れる／切る.
issues.suggestion: Replace this item with “電源ボタンを押して電源を入れる／切る: to turn the power on/off by pressing the power button”.

issues.concern: 押しする is not the correct verb form here.
issues.suggestion: Change the Japanese to 電源ボタンを2秒間押す.

issues.concern: 虚言（きょげん）and 狂言（きょうげん）are not homophones: 狂言 has a long vowel in its first syllable.
issues.suggestion: Replace the final two sentences with: "Do not confuse 虚言（きょげん）with 狂言（きょうげん）, which refers to a traditional Japanese comedic theater form. 狂言 has a long vowel in its first syllable."

issues.concern: "Wanting to worry" incorrectly introduces a desire to worry. 心配するのは分かる means understanding the concern or why someone worries.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "I understand the concern, but I'm careful not to become too controlling."

issues.concern: ふやかす is not used almost exclusively in cooking; it also commonly describes softening things such as nails, scabs, or paper by soaking.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "A transitive godan verb meaning to soften something by soaking, commonly used in cooking."

issues.concern: Although colloquial, ほったらかす can be used in polite speech with forms such as ほったらかしました. Informal vocabulary is not incompatible with polite verb endings.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Generally avoided in formal writing, but can occur in polite conversation."

issues.concern: Cities with administrative wards also have a 市役所; it is not limited to cities without wards.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 市役所: city hall — the administrative office for a city.

issues.concern: “From the morning” is not idiomatic here and can suggest snow that fell in the morning rather than when the shoveling began. 朝から marks the starting time of the activity.
issues.suggestion: I started shoveling snow in the morning.

issues.concern: 中断 does not necessarily mean deliberate stopping; it also describes interruptions caused by accidents, technical failures, or other external circumstances.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 中断: interruption or suspension of an activity — more formal; may be intentional or unintentional"

issues.concern: 転勤 is not restricted to company employees; it also applies to government employees, teachers, and others transferred to a different workplace.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "転勤: job transfer — emphasizes relocation to a different workplace."

issues.concern: 石垣 is not specific to Japanese castles; it also denotes stone walls and retaining walls elsewhere.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 石垣: stone wall — a wall made by stacking stones, including castle walls and retaining walls.

issues.concern: 神経科 is not exclusively neurology and can refer to a specialty treating psychiatric conditions. The note confuses it with 神経内科.
issues.suggestion: Replace this line with: 神経内科: neurology department — treats neurological conditions.

issues.concern: “To administer orally” means to give medication, whereas 服用する means to take medication oneself.
issues.suggestion: Replace with “to take medicine orally”.

issues.concern: 写す does not inherently imply manual transcription; it can also refer to copying mechanically or photographing.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 写す: to copy — can refer to manual transcription as well as other kinds of copying".

issues.concern: 「弁護士が」 marks the lawyer as the person concluding the contract, whereas the English presents the lawyer as a witness. The Japanese appears to contain a particle error.
issues.suggestion: Change the Japanese to 「弁護士の立ち会いのもとで契約を結んだ。」 to match the English.

issues.concern: 涼しい目 normally describes clear, fresh-looking, attractive eyes, not a detached or unimpressed gaze.
issues.suggestion: Remove this comparison or replace 涼しい目 with 冷ややかな目, meaning a cold or disapproving gaze.

issues.concern: The idiom expresses intense fear; it does not denote a body part. 肝 occurs only as part of the figurative expression.
issues.suggestion: Remove "body-part"; retain "emotion".

issues.concern: 寝坊 can also refer to a person who sleeps late or oversleeps, so excluding the person sense is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 寝坊: oversleeping; a person who sleeps late or oversleeps.

issues.concern: 突き抜ける is intransitive. The を marking the barrier or route traversed does not make it transitive.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Intransitive. Takes を to mark the barrier or route passed through."

issues.concern: 経営不振 means poor business performance, not poor management. Also, 解散することになった says dissolution was decided on, not that it had already occurred.
issues.suggestion: Translate as: "It was decided that the company would be dissolved due to poor business performance."

issues.concern: スマホ is not formed by taking the first two mora of a compound word; those would give スマ, not スマホ.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Japanese has many abbreviations formed by combining shortened parts of compound words (e.g., スマホ from スマートフォン)."

issues.concern: 頭文字 means an initial letter or initials, not an acronym.
issues.suggestion: Change "initials, acronym" to "initial letter; initials".

issues.concern: “Frequency” means how often something occurs, whereas 周期 means the interval between repetitions. In scientific usage, period and frequency are reciprocals, not synonyms.
issues.suggestion: Change to “cycle; period; recurring interval”.

issues.concern: 震源 means the earthquake's hypocenter (focus), not its epicenter. The epicenter is on the Earth's surface.
issues.suggestion: The depth of the earthquake's hypocenter was about 10 kilometers.

issues.concern: Hanpen is normally cooked by poaching in hot water, not steaming. The gloss and explanation incorrectly describe its preparation.
issues.suggestion: Change the gloss to "hanpen; soft white fish cake made from fish paste" and replace "steamed" with "poached in hot water" in the explanation.

issues.concern: 貫通する has both intransitive and transitive uses; the categorical claim that it is intransitive is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: State that 貫通する can be intransitive or transitive: トンネルが貫通する illustrates the intransitive use, while 弾丸が壁を貫通する illustrates the transitive use.

issues.concern: The pattern reverses the roles: ～として防犯対策 means crime prevention measures serving as ～, not ～ serving as a crime prevention measure.
issues.suggestion: Replace the bullet with: 「防犯対策として～」 means “～ as a crime prevention measure.”

issues.concern: “His attitude was ... he seemed confident” is an ungrammatical construction, and the hesitation phrase should be “how should I put it,” not “how should I say.”
issues.suggestion: Use: “His manner was, how should I put it, outwardly confident but actually rather anxious.”

issues.concern: 嘘をつく is a standard collocation, but it is not the only way to express telling a lie; 嘘を言う is also valid.
issues.suggestion: Replace the absolute claim with: "嘘をつく is a standard fixed collocation for telling a lie."

issues.concern: おまけに does not imply a negative addition; it can introduce positive information as well.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: おまけに: on top of that; what's more — adds another point, which may be positive or negative.

issues.concern: 現役合格 means gaining admission while still in the final year of school, rather than after spending an extra year preparing. It does not necessarily mean passing on the first attempt; a student may take multiple entrance exams that year.
issues.suggestion: Replace the explanations of 現役合格 in both USAGE and COMMON COLLOCATIONS with 'passing an entrance exam while still in one's final year of school, without an extra preparation year.'

issues.concern: 目を見張る is not restricted to positive amazement; it can also describe widening one's eyes in negative surprise or anger.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Often expresses admiration or wonder, but can also describe widening one's eyes in surprise or anger." Also soften the earlier claim that it is almost always positive.

issues.concern: いくらか does not inherently indicate a smaller degree than 少し. The notes incorrectly present a fixed degree ranking between these near-synonyms.
issues.suggestion: Remove this comparison and the later claim that 少し indicates a 'slightly larger degree.' State instead that いくらか and 少し overlap in meaning, with the degree depending on context.

issues.concern: において is an adverbial form used with a predicate, not a sentence-ending form.
issues.suggestion: Replace “sentence-ending form” with “adverbial form used to modify a predicate,” and revise the corresponding USAGE bullet accordingly.

issues.concern: において is not restricted to “in the context of”; it also marks a physical location where an event occurs, as in 東京において開催する.
issues.suggestion: Change to: “において: in, at — another formal expression for a location or context”.

issues.concern: In くさち, くさ is a kun'yomi reading, but ち is an on'yomi reading of 地.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "The reading くさち combines the kun'yomi くさ for 草 with the on'yomi ち for 地."

issues.concern: 利益 is not purely economic; it can also mean a nonfinancial benefit or advantage.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 利益: profit, benefit, advantage — does not itself imply a legal right".

issues.concern: 作業中 is not restricted to physical or manual work; it also applies to computer-based and mental tasks.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "作業中: working on a task; work in progress".

issues.concern: The etymology incorrectly assigns a meaning-bearing role to 羅. 甲羅 is formed from 甲 (こう) plus the suffix ら; 羅 represents that suffix phonetically.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "甲羅 is formed from 甲 (こう), meaning ‘shell’ or ‘armor,’ plus the suffix ら, written 羅."

issues.concern: “Recycled paper” means paper already reprocessed (再生紙), whereas 古紙 is used or waste paper collected as recycling material.
issues.suggestion: Use “waste paper; used paper” in both the main gloss and definitions[0].gloss.

issues.concern: “These until privatization in 1985” incorrectly includes camphor, whose government monopoly ended in 1962.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: “The Japan Tobacco and Salt Public Corporation (日本専売公社) managed these monopolies, but the camphor monopoly ended in 1962. The corporation was privatized in 1985.”

issues.concern: In Japan, 検視官 is a police role, not a prosecutor's title. Prosecutors can conduct 検視, but that does not make them 検視官.
issues.suggestion: Change the gloss to "death-scene investigating officer (police)".

issues.concern: 妖怪 can refer to uncanny phenomena as well as supernatural beings, so explicitly excluding phenomena is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 妖怪: supernatural being or uncanny phenomenon — often refers to beings associated with strange occurrences".

issues.concern: 服用 means taking medicine by mouth; it is not route-neutral and does not ordinarily include injections or external application.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "- 服用: taking medicine by mouth — a more common term with essentially the same meaning".

issues.concern: 積もっている can describe ongoing accumulation as well as a resulting accumulated state. The explicit exclusion of the progressive reading is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: State that 積もっている can mean either 'has accumulated/is piled up' or 'is accumulating,' depending on context.

issues.concern: 件 also undergoes sound changes after 6 and 8: 六件 is ろっけん, and 八件 can be はっけん.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "As a counter, 件 has contracted pronunciations with 1, 6, 8, and 10: いっけん, ろっけん, はっけん (also はちけん), and じゅっけん／じっけん."

issues.concern: Japanese business cards do not always include a title; people without a formal title commonly omit one.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "Business cards (名刺) often include one's title."

issues.concern: The stated range of 100–400 pages is not a generally accepted length for a novella; its upper end is typical of a full-length novel. Japanese length guidelines often count 400-character manuscript sheets rather than printed pages.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "For sense 1, there is no strict page or word count definition; a 中編小説 is longer than a short story but shorter than a full-length novel."

issues.concern: 頑張ったなのに is ungrammatical: のに attaches directly to the past-tense verb 頑張った, without な.
issues.suggestion: Replace 頑張ったなのに... with 頑張ったのに..., or use a valid なのに example such as 約束した日なのに....

issues.concern: The neutral formality label contradicts the notes' explicit description of the word as formal.
issues.suggestion: Change the formality label to formal.

issues.concern: 秋桜 read as コスモス is not phonetic kanji usage: the characters represent the flower's appearance and season, not the sounds of コスモス.
issues.suggestion: Replace "using ateji (phonetic kanji usage)" with "with the meaning-based kanji spelling 秋桜".

issues.concern: 公文書館 means an archives institution, not specifically a national archives; it can also be a local government archives.
issues.suggestion: Change to 「公文書館 (public archives)」.

issues.concern: Japan's commonest woodpecker is the Japanese pygmy woodpecker (コゲラ), not the great spotted woodpecker (アカゲラ).
issues.suggestion: Change this line to "- アカゲラ: great spotted woodpecker".

issues.concern: The tag "body-part" denotes an anatomical part, but 息をつく denotes breathing or taking a brief rest, not a body part.
issues.suggestion: Remove "body-part" from the semantic tags.

issues.concern: 降り続ける is a normal intransitive expression meaning 'to keep falling,' not a transitive counterpart meaning 'to keep letting fall.' It does not require a volitional subject.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 「降り続ける」 is also commonly used for rain or snow continuing to fall; it is intransitive in this use.

issues.concern: The 15-bout schedule and eight-win threshold apply to wrestlers in the top two divisions, not all sumo wrestlers. Lower-division wrestlers normally have seven bouts and need four wins for 勝ち越し.
issues.suggestion: In sumo's top two divisions, wrestlers normally have 15 bouts per tournament and achieve 勝ち越し with eight or more wins; in lower divisions, they normally have seven bouts and need four wins. A winning record generally leads to a higher ranking.

issues.concern: 初戦 is not restricted to sports; it also means the first battle or engagement in warfare.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 初戦: first match, game, or battle.

issues.concern: The meaning 'to get back at someone by proving oneself' belongs to 見返す（みかえす）, not 見返る（みかえる）. Definition 2 incorrectly conflates these two verbs.
issues.suggestion: Remove this meaning from the main gloss and delete definition 2. Place that sense and examples 3–5 under 見返す.

issues.concern: The notes incorrectly present vindicating oneself as a sense of 見返る. The associated collocations use the different verb 見返す, not conjugations of 見返る.
issues.suggestion: Remove the second-sense discussion and its collocations, and explain that 見返す is a separate verb meaning, among other things, to prove one's detractors wrong.

issues.concern: The neutral formality label contradicts the notes' explicit description of a somewhat formal register.
issues.suggestion: Change the formality label to formal.

issues.concern: 英雄的 describes heroic qualities or conduct, not an emotion.
issues.suggestion: Remove the "emotion" tag.

issues.concern: 注力する does not take 経営資源 as a direct object. This collocation incorrectly models its argument structure.
issues.suggestion: Replace with 「経営資源を投入する: to commit business resources」 or 「重点分野に注力する: to focus efforts on priority areas」.

issues.concern: 休刊日 is not restricted to coordinated newspaper holidays; it can refer to an individual publication's non-publication day.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "A day when a newspaper or other periodical is not published, often referring to coordinated newspaper holidays in Japan."

issues.concern: Coordinated newspaper holidays are not unique to Japan; newspapers in Taiwan also observe shared publication breaks around Lunar New Year.
issues.suggestion: Remove the claim of uniqueness: "This practice reflects the newspaper industry's labor agreements."

issues.concern: なき is the classical attributive form of the adjective なし, not a classical negative form of the verb ある.
issues.suggestion: Replace the explanation of なき with "the classical attributive form of なし, meaning ‘nonexistent’ or ‘without’."

issues.concern: 殴り倒す is not restricted to blows with fists; it can also involve striking with a stick or another object.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "- 殴り倒す: to knock down by striking or punching".

issues.concern: 仕立て直す takes the garment being remade as its object, not its size. サイズを仕立て直す teaches an incorrect collocation.
issues.suggestion: Replace with 「サイズに合わせて仕立て直す: to alter a garment to fit」.

issues.concern: 諸事情 means various circumstances or reasons, not communication. Its use in announcements or explanations does not make communication its semantic domain.
issues.suggestion: Replace "communication" with "abstract".

issues.concern: The morphological derivation is incorrect: しない is not a negative suffix attached to 果てる here.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Formed from 果て (end) + the emphatic particle し + ない (nonexistent); literally, 'having no end.'"

issues.concern: 沸騰 means boiling, not specifically a rolling boil at 100°C. The boiling temperature depends on the liquid and pressure, and boiling need not be vigorous.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "In cooking contexts, 沸騰 explicitly describes boiling, while 沸く is a more everyday expression for water coming to a boil."

issues.concern: Four knocks are not generally considered excessive; four is also recognized as a formal etiquette convention.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Two knocks are often associated with checking a restroom stall. Three knocks are common in Japanese business settings, while four are also accepted as a formal convention."

issues.concern: 宗家 denotes the head house or head of a traditional-art lineage, not the school itself. "Founding school" misleadingly equates 宗家 with 流派; the same wording also appears in the overall gloss.
issues.suggestion: Use "head house; grand master of a traditional art" and revise the explanation to distinguish the head house or person from the school.

issues.concern: The Japanese refers to visiting a head house or grand master, not a founding school.
issues.suggestion: I visited the head house of a tea ceremony lineage.

issues.concern: 宗家に弟子入りした means becoming a disciple of the head master, not of a founding school.
issues.suggestion: I became a disciple of the grand master of a karate lineage.

issues.concern: "Founding schools" misrepresents 三大宗家, which refers to the three major head houses.
issues.suggestion: Urasenke is one of the three major head houses of tea ceremony.

issues.concern: 毎週 can modify nouns referring to recurring events when followed by の, as in 毎週の会議.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 「毎週: every week — used adverbially or with の to modify a noun, as in 毎週の会議」.

issues.concern: The Japan Mint's Tokyo branch relocated to Saitama in 2016; its current branches are in Saitama and Hiroshima.
issues.suggestion: Replace "branches in Tokyo and Hiroshima" with "branches in Saitama and Hiroshima".

issues.concern: The Bank of Japan issues banknotes but does not print them. Banknotes are printed by the National Printing Bureau.
issues.suggestion: Replace "prints paper currency (banknotes)" with "issues paper currency (banknotes)".

issues.concern: This conflates school dismissal announcements with municipal neighborhood broadcasts reminding children playing outside to go home. Those broadcasts do not generally announce an elementary school's 下校時間.
issues.suggestion: Remove this sentence, or clarify that neighborhood broadcasts reminding children to go home are distinct from school dismissal times.

issues.concern: 歩合給の割合 refers to the proportion of total pay made up of commission, not the commission rate applied to sales.
issues.suggestion: Since commission makes up a large proportion of the pay, income drops significantly in months with low sales.

issues.concern: This equates the share of pay derived from commission with the commission rate, which is a different percentage.
issues.suggestion: Change the translation to "proportion of pay made up of commission".

issues.concern: 最高値 can also be read さいこうち when it means the highest numerical value, so categorically rejecting that reading is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: State that 最高値 is read さいこうね for market prices and さいこうち for numerical values more generally. In the following sentence, explicitly distinguish 値 read as ね from 値 read as ち.

issues.concern: The neutral formality label contradicts the notes' explicit description of the word as formal.
issues.suggestion: Change the formality label to formal.

issues.concern: 引き落とし does not mean specifically non-automatic withdrawal; it commonly refers to automatic debits as well.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 引き落とし — withdrawal/debit (also commonly used for automatic debits)"

issues.concern: The change from はん to ぱん is 半濁音化 (h→p), not rendaku (sequential voicing).
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "The reading is しんぱん (with 版 pronounced ぱん after ん)."

issues.concern: 鮮魚 refers to fresh, uncooked fish, not cooked fish that happens to be fresh.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 鮮魚 — fresh, uncooked fish (emphasis on freshness).

issues.concern: Japanese マグマ is conventionally traced to German Magma, not English.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "A loanword from German Magma, ultimately from Greek."

issues.concern: 視聴者 means a viewer or audience member, not a subscriber. It does not imply a subscription.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 視聴者: viewer — audience member for TV or video content.

issues.concern: ロマンチック is not an English borrowing transmitted via German romantisch; the stated borrowing route is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Remove the German intermediary claim: “A loanword from English ‘romantic’.”

issues.concern: The expression describes cognitive quickness, not society or social phenomena.
issues.suggestion: Replace "society" with "cognition".

issues.concern: ニキビ denotes a skin lesion or acne, not an anatomical body part.
issues.suggestion: Remove "body-part"; retain "health".

issues.concern: 超特急 predates the Shinkansen; the term was already used for the prewar 燕 service, introduced in 1930.
issues.suggestion: Replace the origin claim with: "The term has been used for Shinkansen services."

issues.concern: Neither "body-part" nor "cognition" fits むせ返る: it describes choking or being physically overwhelmed by intense sensory conditions, not an anatomical part or a cognitive process.
issues.suggestion: Remove "body-part" and "cognition".

issues.concern: 庭園 does not specify that a garden is at ground level; it can also refer to a rooftop garden.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 庭園: garden — the general term, without specifying its location".

issues.concern: 新型 does not necessarily mean a completely new design; it can also be an improved version of an earlier model.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 新型: new model — a new type or model, which may incorporate improvements to an earlier one.

issues.concern: “Realism” and “immersiveness” are meanings of 臨場感, not of 臨場 itself. Presenting them as a sense of 臨場 teaches a misleading standalone meaning.
issues.suggestion: Remove this sense and “sense of being there” from the main gloss. Keep 臨場感 and its meaning in the compound notes and examples.

issues.concern: “Opening up spaces” conflates 解放する with its homophone 開放する. Opening a space or making it accessible is normally 開放する, not 解放する.
issues.suggestion: Remove “opening up spaces” from the examples of physical liberation.

issues.concern: The stated word order is reversed relative to the example: 三日連続 is a duration expression followed by 連続.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "Often used after a duration expression: duration＋連続 (e.g., 三日連続 — three days running)."

issues.concern: 達成する is not restricted almost exclusively to 目標; other common objects include 目的, ノルマ, and numerical targets.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Commonly takes objects such as 目標 (goal), 目的 (objective), and ノルマ (quota)."

issues.concern: 車掌 contains 掌, not 長, so it does not share the stated 長 pattern.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 車掌 — train conductor (a different transport role).

issues.concern: The rope was removed from senior individual competition in 2011, not from all senior events. Senior group competition used ropes afterward, including in 2017–2018.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "Senior individual competition uses four apparatus; rope was removed from senior individual events in 2011 but has appeared in senior group competition since then."

issues.concern: This incorrectly implies that registered given names must use kanji from these lists. Hiragana and katakana are also permitted.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "When using kanji in a child's registered given name, parents must choose from the 人名用漢字 or 常用漢字; hiragana and katakana are also permitted."

issues.concern: The explanation incorrectly says 単色 excludes patterns and gradients. Single-color printing, for example, can include patterns and tonal gradations using one ink.
issues.suggestion: Change the explanation to: "Using or consisting of a single color."

issues.concern: 度に is the kanji spelling of たびに, not a separate, more literary or formal expression.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 「度に（たびに）: an alternative spelling of たびに, with the same meaning and usage.」

issues.concern: “Plastic bags became paid” is not idiomatic English for bags no longer being free; it misleadingly models “became paid” as meaning “began to cost money.”
issues.suggestion: “Since stores started charging for plastic bags, I make sure not to forget my shopping bag.”

issues.concern: 窓の外 means 'outside the window,' not the window itself.
issues.suggestion: I looked out the window.

issues.concern: 冬眠 can be used figuratively for prolonged inactivity, including a company's inactivity; the categorical exclusion is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "冬眠: hibernation — primarily winter dormancy in animals; also used figuratively for prolonged inactivity."

issues.concern: Junmai can combine with ginjo and daiginjo, but not honjozo: honjozo requires added brewing alcohol, whereas junmai excludes it.
issues.suggestion: Change the parenthetical to “can be combined with ginjo or daiginjo.”

issues.concern: In standard sake terminology, 冷や means room temperature, not chilled.
issues.suggestion: Use “吟醸酒を冷やして飲む: to drink ginjo sake chilled,” or translate the existing phrase as “to drink ginjo sake at room temperature.”

issues.concern: Not all ores are minerals. Ore can be rock containing economically extractable minerals, whereas 鉱物 refers to minerals themselves.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 鉱物: mineral — a naturally occurring substance; ore is rock or mineral material from which valuable constituents can be extracted economically"

issues.concern: Not all Japanese banks offer time deposits; some, such as Lawson Bank, offer ordinary deposits but not time deposits.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "A basic financial product offered by many Japanese banks."

issues.concern: The explanation incorrectly claims that 届け物 implies a personal or thoughtful delivery rather than commercial shipping. It can refer neutrally to commercially delivered items as well.
issues.suggestion: Remove the sentence asserting this distinction; retain the explanation that it is an item delivered or sent to someone.

issues.concern: 四拍子 is also used figuratively, as in 四拍子揃う, to describe four favorable qualities being present.
issues.suggestion: Remove “musical only, no figurative use,” or state that 四拍子 can also refer figuratively to four qualities.

issues.concern: 取り立て does not generally mean 'freshly made'; its freshness sense refers to something just picked, caught, or obtained.
issues.suggestion: Change to 'collection (of debts); freshly picked/caught'.

issues.concern: 'Freshly made' incorrectly extends the meaning of 取り立て to newly produced things in general.
issues.suggestion: Remove 'freshly made' from the gloss and 'or made' from the explanation.

issues.concern: 訓読文 is a text rendered into Japanese through kundoku, essentially a 書き下し文, not the Chinese text with reading marks added. The latter is called 訓点文.
issues.suggestion: Replace 訓読文 with 訓点文 in item 2.

issues.concern: The chin is not propped on the elbow. 肘をつく means resting one's elbow or elbows on a surface; it does not itself specify supporting the chin.
issues.suggestion: to rest one's elbow(s) on a table or other surface

issues.concern: The chin is not propped on the elbow. The second gloss incorrectly describes both the posture and the meaning of 肘をつく.
issues.suggestion: to rest one's elbow(s) on a table or other surface

issues.concern: 頬杖 means supporting one's chin or cheek with one's hand, with the elbow resting on a surface—not resting the chin on the elbow.
issues.suggestion: I was tired and resting my chin in my hand with my elbow propped up.

issues.concern: Rayon is classified as 再生繊維 (regenerated fiber), not 合成繊維. Listing it under types of 合成繊維 is misleading despite the parenthetical qualification.
issues.suggestion: Remove rayon from TYPES, or identify it separately as レーヨン: rayon, a regenerated fiber (再生繊維), not 合成繊維.

issues.concern: Japan had legally adopted 満年齢 before 1950. The law effective in 1950 promoted its everyday use rather than introducing it as the official age system.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "A law effective in 1950 encouraged the use of 満年齢 instead of customary 数え年, but 数え年 is still used for some traditional observances, including 厄年 and 還暦."

issues.concern: 敬白 is not exclusively paired with 謹啓; it can also close letters beginning with other highly formal openings, such as 恭啓.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Commonly paired with the opening 謹啓."

issues.concern: 敬白 is not the only closing used with 謹啓; 謹言 and 謹白 are also standard pairings.
issues.suggestion: Replace with "Commonly paired with closings such as 敬白, 謹言, or 謹白." Also remove the exclusive pairing claim from the definition's explanation.

issues.concern: 着地する means to land, not to dismount, and 平均台で does not mean 'from the balance beam.'
issues.suggestion: Replace with「平均台から下りる: to dismount from the balance beam」.

issues.concern: 注油する denotes the action of oiling or lubricating, not a tool.
issues.suggestion: Remove the semantic tag "tool".

issues.concern: 時効が消滅する does not mean that the limitation period expires. It says that the limitation itself ceases to exist.
issues.suggestion: Remove this collocation. For expiration of a limitation period, use 時効が完成する.

issues.concern: 印象的な can describe negative or disturbing things that leave a strong impression; it is not restricted to positive or neutral connotations.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Describes something that creates a lasting impression, whether positive, neutral, or negative."

issues.concern: Four tiers do not avoid the unlucky number four. The traditional avoidance concerns how the fourth tier is named.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "Traditional sets have four or five tiers, though three-tier sets are most common today. The fourth tier is traditionally called 与の重 rather than 四の重 to avoid the unlucky association of 四."

issues.concern: 弁当箱 are not necessarily single-compartment containers; they can have multiple compartments or stacking tiers.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 弁当箱: lunch box — a container for a packed meal, which may have compartments or stacking tiers"

issues.concern: 発火点 means ignition temperature (autoignition temperature), not flash point. Flash point is 引火点.
issues.suggestion: Change the line to 「- 発火点: ignition temperature / autoignition temperature」.

issues.concern: 賃貸 means renting something out for payment; it is not restricted to renting an entire apartment or house and can also apply to rooms, commercial premises, and other property.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 賃貸: rental / letting — renting out property for payment".

issues.concern: The characters in 真面目 were not chosen for their sounds to spell まじめ. This is a meaning-based spelling with a special whole-word reading.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "真面目 read as まじめ is a meaning-based spelling with a whole-word reading (熟字訓), rather than a combination of the characters’ usual readings."

issues.concern: This confuses 消却 with 償却. 償却 means amortization or depreciation; 消却 can mean cancellation or destruction, including destruction by burning, so its meaning is not completely different from 焼却.
issues.suggestion: Replace this item with: '- 償却: depreciation / amortization — a financial term pronounced しょうきゃく.'

issues.concern: 調印する is not restricted to international agreements or treaties; it is also used for contracts and other formal agreements.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "調印する: to formally sign a treaty, contract, or agreement".

issues.concern: The etymology reverses the components' meanings: 引っ切り refers to cutting off or interruption, not rapid succession; なし negates that interruption.
issues.suggestion: Replace the etymology with: "From 引っ切り (cutting off; interruption) + なし (without): literally, without interruption."

issues.concern: 当社比 indicates a comparison with the company's own products or figures, not with the company itself.
issues.suggestion: Change the gloss to "compared with our own products or previous figures."

issues.concern: 無色 means lacking color, not being transparent. Transparency is a separate property expressed by 透明.
issues.suggestion: Remove “transparent”: “colorless; uncolored”.

issues.concern: 皇位 is not restricted to the Japanese emperor; it can also refer to the throne or position of an emperor elsewhere, such as a Chinese emperor.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "It refers to an emperor's position or throne, commonly that of the Japanese Emperor (天皇)."

issues.concern: The claim about こじれる is too narrow. こじれる is also commonly used for an illness that worsens or drags on (風邪がこじれる), so it is not limited to situations or relationships.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase as: こじれる: to get complicated or worse, often for relationships, negotiations or an illness that drags on (風邪がこじれる).

issues.concern: 扶養 means the act of supporting someone. It does not mean 'dependents' (the people supported); that is 扶養家族. Listing 'dependents' as a gloss could lead learners to use 扶養 as a noun for people.
issues.suggestion: support; maintenance; providing for dependents

issues.concern: 精錬 primarily means refining a crude metal into a purer one. Extracting metal from ore is more precisely 製錬 (smelting). Defining 精錬 as 'specifically extracting metal from ore' likely misstates its core meaning.
issues.suggestion: - 精錬: (metal) refining — purifying crude metal; cf. 製錬 (smelting), extracting metal from ore

issues.concern: This sentence limits 区役所 to designated cities (政令指定都市). Tokyo's 23 special wards (特別区) also each have a 区役所, e.g. 新宿区役所, and they are not part of any designated city.
issues.suggestion: The administrative center for a 区 (ward), either in a designated city or one of Tokyo's 23 special wards.

issues.concern: 口コミ is usually explained as a play on マスコミ (mass communication), coined to mean communication by mouth. Calling it an abbreviation of a word '口コミュニケーション' misstates its origin, since no such established word exists.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 口コミ (a coinage modeled on マスコミ, meaning communication by word of mouth)

issues.concern: No well-known comedian or 替え歌 performer named 'Hiro Iki' exists; the name appears to be garbled or invented. The performer most famous for 替え歌 is 嘉門達夫 (Kamon Tatsuo).
issues.suggestion: Replace 'Hiro Iki' with 'Kamon Tatsuo (嘉門タツオ)', or drop the name.

issues.concern: Major Japanese dictionaries (e.g. Daijisen, Daijirin) trace シロップ to Dutch 'siroop', or to both Dutch and English. It entered Japanese through Dutch medical vocabulary. Attributing it only to English is likely inaccurate.
issues.suggestion: From Dutch "siroop" (also associated with English "syrup").

issues.concern: 泣きつく does not usually involve physical clinging. It normally means tearfully begging someone or running to them for help, e.g. 親に泣きつく. Calling it 'physically emotional begging' misleads learners.
issues.suggestion: Change to: '泣きつく: to go crying to someone for help; to beg tearfully — colloquial, implies dependence on the listener'

issues.concern: In Japanese usage, トレッキング means walking through mountain areas without aiming for the summit, and it is often a day trip. Defining it as 'multi-day walks' adds a restriction the word does not have.
issues.suggestion: トレッキング: trekking — walking through mountain areas (often without aiming for a summit); can be a day trip or longer

issues.concern: 突然の知らせ uses 突然 as a の-adjective (noun + の), not a な-adjective. 突然な is non-standard or rare, so calling this a な-adjective modifier misleads learners about which particle to use.
issues.suggestion: 突然 can also modify nouns with の (as a noun/の-adjective): 突然の知らせ (a sudden notification).

issues.concern: 十分 in 十分蒸らしてください is most naturally read as じゅうぶん ('thoroughly'), not じゅっぷん ('ten minutes'). The translation adds a specific duration the Japanese may not state.
issues.suggestion: Once the rice finishes cooking, let it steam thoroughly. (Or write 10分 in the Japanese if ten minutes is intended.)

issues.concern: The contrast suggests 散布する is limited to liquids. In fact 散布 is used just as readily for powders, granules, seeds and leaflets, as the entry's own explanation and collocations (肥料, ビラ) show.
issues.suggestion: Reword, e.g. '散らす: to scatter — more general everyday verb, not limited to deliberate distribution over an area.'

issues.concern: 「奇才の才人」 is not a common collocation. It is a redundant, unnatural pairing, and listing it under COMMON COLLOCATIONS would mislead learners.
issues.suggestion: Remove it, or replace it with a real collocation such as 「当代きっての才人」 (one of the most talented people of the day).

issues.concern: Overstates the restriction to 本格的/本格的に. 本格 is also very common in other compounds and prefix uses, such as 本格化, 本格派, 本格始動, 本格参入, 本格ミステリー and 本格焼酎. The notes themselves list 本格派.
issues.suggestion: Most often used as 本格的 (na-adjective) or 本格的に (adverb), and in compounds such as 本格化, 本格派 and 本格始動; rarely used as a standalone noun.

issues.concern: 名残惜しい is the standard, everyday word for reluctance to part. It is common in ordinary speech and set phrases such as 名残惜しいですが…, so it is not 'more literary'. 別れ惜しい is a less established, colloquial coinage; 別れが惜しい or 別れを惜しむ are the usual phrasings. The contrast misleads learners about which form is standard.
issues.suggestion: Describe 名残惜しい as the standard, common near-synonym rather than more literary. Optionally note that 別れが惜しい is the more common phrasing.

issues.concern: The notes call 重篤 the most severe level of illness, but they later say 危篤 is even more severe. Also, 重篤 is not a level on the standard 軽症/中等症/重症 grading scale; it is a descriptive term for a grave, possibly life-threatening condition.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase as 'A formal medical term for an extremely severe, potentially life-threatening condition.' Present the 軽症→中等症→重症 scale separately, noting that 重篤 describes conditions beyond 重症 and 危篤 means imminent death.

issues.concern: 開幕戦 is not limited to a league season. It also names the opening match of a tournament or event, such as the World Cup 開幕戦. 'Specifically the season opener' is too restrictive.
issues.suggestion: 開幕戦: opening game (of a season, tournament, or event), i.e. the first game of the whole event, not each team's first match

issues.concern: 論文 is not more formal than 論考. 論文 is the standard everyday term (e.g. 卒業論文), and 論考 is the more literary, elevated word. 論文 also covers essays and theses, not only research papers.
issues.suggestion: 論文: thesis, academic paper — the standard, common term for academic papers; 論考 is more literary and less common

issues.concern: The origin is misdescribed. In Zen texts such as the Linji record (老婆心切), the term describes a master's earnest, painstaking kindness toward disciples, likened to an old woman's solicitude. It does not describe a grandmother's compassion for her grandchildren.
issues.suggestion: Originally from Zen Buddhist texts, describing a teacher's earnest, painstaking kindness toward disciples, likened to an old woman's solicitude.

issues.concern: 洞窟 is the standard everyday word for 'cave', not a scientific term. Calling it 'the scientific term' would mislead learners about its register and frequency.
issues.suggestion: Has a more natural, literary feel than the standard term 洞窟.

issues.concern: 毒ガスマスク is not a standard collocation for 'gas mask'. The usual Japanese terms are 防毒マスク and ガスマスク.
issues.suggestion: Replace with '防毒マスク / ガスマスク: gas mask' (listed as related words rather than as a 毒ガス collocation).

issues.concern: This line lists 値 with the meaning 'price' but gives no reading. The entry itself is 値 (あたい), whose meaning is not 'price', so a learner may read this as a claim about あたい. The 'price' meaning belongs only to the reading ね.
issues.suggestion: Add the reading: '値（ね）: price (everyday word for the cost of goods)'.

issues.concern: 幻想的 means dreamlike or magical. In everyday English 'fantastic' usually means 'great/wonderful', so a learner may take 幻想的 to mean 'amazing'.
issues.suggestion: The radiance of the morning sun reflected on the lake's surface, creating a dreamlike (magical) scene.

issues.concern: 'Almost exclusively' overstates the restriction. 漆黒の + noun is the dominant pattern, but 漆黒 also appears as a standalone noun (辺りは漆黒に包まれた, 漆黒に染まる) and predicatively (髪は漆黒だ).
issues.suggestion: Change to 'Most commonly used as a modifier before a noun: 漆黒の + noun', and optionally note uses such as 漆黒に包まれる.

issues.concern: Without any context, 今日は低気圧だね most naturally refers to the weather (low pressure today, often said when complaining of headaches). Translating it only as 'You seem to be in a bad mood' presents the figurative reading as the default, which could mislead learners.
issues.suggestion: Add context that makes the mood sense clear, e.g. 課長、今日は低気圧だね。 'The section chief seems to be in a bad mood today.'

issues.concern: The Japanese sentence uses 水深深度, which is a redundant, non-standard compound (水深 already means 'water depth'). Learners may copy it as if it were a real term.
issues.suggestion: Use natural Japanese such as 「湖の深度を計測する。」 (To measure the depth of the lake.) or 「海底の深度を計測する。」

issues.concern: "within next week" is unnatural English and a common learner error; 来週中に means sometime during next week.
issues.suggestion: The results of the document screening will be sent by email sometime next week.

issues.concern: The Spanish Armada is conventionally called 無敵艦隊, a compound without の. Presenting 無敵の艦隊 as its name misstates the standard term.
issues.suggestion: Change to '無敵艦隊: the Invincible Armada (the Spanish Armada)'.

issues.concern: Sense 1 of 触発 is narrowly 'to detonate on contact' (e.g. 触発機雷, contact mine). Triggering by earthquakes or other events is normally expressed with 誘発 (地震が誘発した地すべり), not 触発. The notes overstate the physical sense's range.
issues.suggestion: Limit sense 1 to detonation on contact (e.g. mines and explosives), and note that 誘発する is the usual verb for an earthquake triggering landslides.
