issues.concern: “Seventh death anniversary” incorrectly places the observance seven years after death and contradicts the correct timing given in the rest of the definition.
issues.suggestion: Use “Buddhist memorial service held six years after a death”.

issues.concern: “Thirteenth death anniversary” means thirteen years after the death, but 十三回忌 is observed twelve years after it.
issues.suggestion: Use “thirteenth-year Buddhist memorial service.”

issues.concern: “Thirteenth death anniversary” contradicts the correct timing given in the remainder of the gloss: twelve years after death.
issues.suggestion: Use “thirteenth-year memorial service, held twelve years after a death.”

issues.concern: The prefix お is customary but not obligatory; 色直し also exists as an unprefixed noun with this meaning.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "The polite お prefix is usually included."

issues.concern: The explanation incorrectly excludes falling drops. たらたら can describe liquid dripping in successive drops, not only running in an unbroken trickle.
issues.suggestion: Change the explanation to: "Liquid trickling or dripping continuously, such as sweat, blood, oil, or sauce."

issues.concern: たらたら does not have to follow the noun directly in the figurative sense. It can function adverbially after a particle, as in 言い訳をたらたらと並べる.
issues.suggestion: Say that たらたら can follow the noun directly or function adverbially with a verb.

issues.concern: パンプス are not restricted to low or medium heels; they can also have high heels.
issues.suggestion: Change to "- パンプス: pumps — court shoes with various heel heights".

issues.concern: くちゃくちゃ is not food-only; it can also describe things being crumpled, rumpled, or disordered.
issues.suggestion: Remove “(food-only)”.

issues.concern: 坊っちゃん is the title of Natsume Sōseki's novel, not its setting. The novel is set mainly in Matsuyama.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "- 坊(ぼ)っちゃん: Natsume Sōseki's famous novel, set mainly in Matsuyama".

issues.concern: The reading given for 酢飯 is incorrect: it is すめし, not めし.
issues.suggestion: Change 酢飯(めし) to 酢飯(すめし).

issues.concern: 苛立たしい can describe the feeling of irritation itself, as in 苛立たしい思い, not only its source.
issues.suggestion: State that 苛立たしい can describe either feeling irritated or something that causes irritation.

issues.concern: 崩れ落ちる is also commonly used of people collapsing, for example from shock, despair, or loss of strength. Saying it is usually for structures, not people, misleadingly discourages a normal use.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- 崩(くず)れ落(お)ちる: to crumble or collapse — used of structures giving way or people collapsing".

issues.concern: ばくばく describes eating behavior or heart pounding; it does not name a food.
issues.suggestion: Remove the semantic tag "food".

issues.concern: The neutral formality label contradicts the notes' explicit description of the word as formal.
issues.suggestion: Change the formality label to formal.

issues.concern: The 50-yen coin also has a hole in the center, so the five-yen coin is not the only Japanese coin with one.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "The five-yen coin is made of brass and has a hole in the center, as does the 50-yen coin."

issues.concern: The explanation confuses 喪中 (mourning) with 忌中. In Japanese Buddhist custom, 49 days normally refers to 忌中; 喪中 commonly lasts about a year.
issues.suggestion: Replace the final sentence with: "In Japan, mourning is commonly observed for about a year; the Buddhist 忌中 period typically lasts 49 days."

issues.concern: がらがら describes a place with very few people or things, not necessarily a completely empty one. It is not inherently stronger than すかすか.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 「- がらがら: nearly empty; very uncrowded (room, train)」.

issues.concern: イルミネーション is not restricted to large public LED installations; it also includes smaller decorative displays and lighting using non-LED bulbs.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "In Japan, イルミネーション refers to decorative lighting displays, particularly popular in winter."

issues.concern: 一分 meaning one draw is read いちぶ, not いっぷん. いっぷん means one minute.
issues.suggestion: Change 一分(いっぷん) to 一分(いちぶ).

issues.concern: 三十三回忌 is observed 32 years after death, not on the thirty-third death anniversary.
issues.suggestion: Use "thirty-second death anniversary; 33rd-year memorial service".

issues.concern: The gloss and explanation incorrectly call this the 33rd anniversary. Counting the year of death as the first year makes 三十三回忌 the 32nd anniversary.
issues.suggestion: Change the gloss to "thirty-second death anniversary; 33rd-year memorial service" and the explanation to say it is held 32 years after death.

issues.concern: "33rd death anniversary" places the rite one year later than 三十三回忌.
issues.suggestion: The family gathered at the temple to hold the memorial service marking the 32nd anniversary of the death.

issues.concern: The explanation incorrectly lists bone density among the measurements. Body composition scales may estimate bone mass, but they do not measure bone density.
issues.suggestion: Replace "bone density" with "estimated bone mass" in the explanation.

issues.concern: 普通自動二輪車 includes motorcycles with an engine displacement of exactly 400cc; “under 400cc” incorrectly excludes them.
issues.suggestion: Change “under 400cc” to “up to and including 400cc”.

issues.concern: ストッキング can also refer to waist-high pantyhose, so it does not exclude waist coverage.
issues.suggestion: Change to: ストッキング: stockings; also commonly used for pantyhose.

issues.concern: らしい does not necessarily imply evidence from other people's reports; it can express inference from other indirect evidence.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "- らしい: hearsay or inference based on indirect evidence; also expresses characteristic qualities"

issues.concern: 生理用品 is a broader term for menstrual products, not an abbreviated form of 生理用ナプキン.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: "The broader term 生理用品(せいりようひん) refers to menstrual products generally."

issues.concern: 湯炊き means cooking rice by adding it to already boiling water; it does not specifically mean boiling in excess water and draining. That method is 湯取り法.
issues.suggestion: Change to "rice cooking starting with boiling water".

issues.concern: The definition incorrectly makes excess water and draining defining features of 湯炊き. The defining feature is putting rice into water that is already boiling.
issues.suggestion: Change the gloss to "rice cooking starting with boiling water" and explain that rice is added to boiling water rather than heated from cold water.

issues.concern: The translation introduces draining, which 湯炊き does not entail.
issues.suggestion: Change to "I ate rice cooked by adding it to boiling water."

issues.concern: The translation incorrectly identifies 湯炊き as the boil-and-drain method.
issues.suggestion: Change to "Adding rice to boiling water is a traditional way to cook rice without a rice cooker."

issues.concern: This contrast incorrectly implies that 湯炊き necessarily involves draining and is opposed to absorption cooking. Its relevant contrast is with starting rice in cold water.
issues.suggestion: Replace with "Contrasts with 水炊き, in which rice and cold water are heated together; in 湯炊き, rice is added after the water boils."

issues.concern: The collocation's English explanation incorrectly equates 湯炊き with the boil-and-drain method.
issues.suggestion: Change the explanation to "to cook rice by adding it to boiling water".

issues.concern: につきまして is not a contracted form. Adding は marks the topic or contrast; it does not undo a contraction.
issues.suggestion: Replace “the contracted form” with “the form”.

issues.concern: ミシン目 refers to a line of perforations, not a tool.
issues.suggestion: Remove the semantic tag "tool".

issues.concern: The list is not in the order of the 六曜 cycle.
issues.suggestion: Reorder the list to 先勝 → 友引 → 先負 → 仏滅 → 大安 → 赤口.

issues.concern: The standard form with する is せねばならない, not しねばならない. Presenting both as interchangeable teaches an incorrect standard conjugation.
issues.suggestion: Change the line to 「- する → せねばならない (must do)」.

issues.concern: The して in すでにして is a connective particle, not the te-form of する.
issues.suggestion: Replace “して (connective te-form)” with “the connective particle して.”

issues.concern: Japan has three types of architect license, not just the two listed: 木造建築士 is also a recognized license category.
issues.suggestion: State that Japan's architect licensing system has three categories: 一級建築士 (national license), 二級建築士 (prefectural license), and 木造建築士 (prefectural license for wooden buildings within specified limits).

issues.concern: This line calls 壺(つぼ) a separate word to avoid confusing with ツボ. The notes themselves say 壺 is the underlying kanji of ツボ, and the pressure-point sense is usually explained as an extension of 壺 'pot'. The line contradicts the entry and misleads learners.
issues.suggestion: Drop 壺 from the 'not to be confused' line and keep only 坪(つぼ). Optionally add that ツボ is the same word as 壺 'pot/jar', usually written in katakana in these senses.

issues.concern: 噛み合わせ is the noun form of the transitive verb 噛み合わせる, not of 噛み合う. The noun from 噛み合う is 噛み合い.
issues.suggestion: Noun form of 噛(か)み合(あ)わせる (to make mesh, to fit together); related to intransitive 噛(か)み合(あ)う (to mesh).

issues.concern: 描(か)く and 描(えが)く are generally treated as distinct verbs that share a kanji: えがく derives from 絵(え)+かく, and dictionaries list them as separate entries. Calling them 'the same verb in dictionary terms' is misleading.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase as: '描(か)く and 描(えが)く are written with the same kanji but are distinct words that differ in nuance:'

issues.concern: Wrong origin language. アジア was not borrowed from English; its pronunciation (ajia) follows the Latin/Romance form Asia, and the word was established in Japanese long before English loans, written in ateji as 亜細亜.
issues.suggestion: Change '(Asia, from English)' to '(Asia, from Latin/Portuguese Asia)' or simply '(Asia)'.

issues.concern: 結婚式 does not belong in a list of 'style/type words.' The 式 in 結婚式 means 'ceremony,' a different sense from the 'style/system' 式 in 西洋式 and 日本式.
issues.suggestion: Remove 結婚式 from this list, or say explicitly that 式 also has a separate 'ceremony' sense (結婚式, 卒業式).

issues.concern: The standard term for Japanese descent is 日系(にっけい), as in 日系アメリカ人. 日本系 is not the normal form, so the note teaches a non-standard word.
issues.suggestion: Replace 日本(にほん)系(けい) with 日系(にっけい), noting its special reading.

issues.concern: 投票 is not a slip or form. It means 'voting; casting a ballot' (a suru-verb), so it is a poor example of 〜票 naming a slip.
issues.suggestion: Replace 投票 with a real slip/form compound such as 住民票(じゅうみんひょう) (certificate of residence) or 調査票(ちょうさひょう) (questionnaire form).

issues.concern: The reading of 一割 is wrong. 一割引き is read いちわりびき, not いっわりびき; 一 does not geminate before わ.
issues.suggestion: Change the reading to 一(いち)割(わり)引(び)き.

issues.concern: 学割 is already short for 学生割引 (student discount), so adding 引き makes it redundant. 学割引き is not a standard compound.
issues.suggestion: Replace with 学割(がくわり) or 学生(がくせい)割引(わりびき), or remove the line.

issues.concern: The reading of 前編 is wrong. It is read ぜんぺん, with 編 changing to ぺん, not ぜんへん. The same wrong reading also appears in the opening paragraph.
issues.suggestion: Change the reading to 前(ぜん)編(ぺん) here and in the first paragraph, and note that 編 becomes ぺん after ん in this compound.

issues.concern: Two-story is the most common form for detached houses in Japan, but not for urban housing overall. Apartments and condominiums (共同住宅) make up most housing in Japanese cities.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 'two-story (the most common form for detached houses)'

issues.concern: 高層階建て is not an established word. 高層 is not a number and cannot fill the 〜階建て slot, so listing it as a related word for 'high-rise building' misleads learners.
issues.suggestion: Remove 高層階建て and list only 高層(こうそう)ビル (or 高層建築(こうそうけんちく)) for 'high-rise building'.

issues.concern: This implies Japanese law required elevators from six floors up. The five-floor walk-up limit for 団地 came from public-housing design standards, not a statutory rule. The Building Standards Act's elevator requirement applies to buildings over 31 m.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase to say public-housing design standards of the time treated five floors as the maximum for buildings without elevators.

issues.concern: 交通費 is formed with the suffix 費(ひ), not 代(だい), so it is a wrong example of a 代 compound.
issues.suggestion: Replace 交通(こうつう)費(ひ) with a genuine 代 compound such as 食事(しょくじ)代(だい) or 部屋(へや)代(だい), or note that 費 is a different suffix.

issues.concern: The Japanese contrasts 傷害致死 with bare 致傷, but the English adds 'assault' and renders 致傷 as 'assault causing injury'. That offense does not exist, since 傷害 is itself the injury offense. The translation adds information and implies a non-existent crime name.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite the example to contrast real offenses, e.g. 強盗致死と強盗致傷は量刑が異なる → 'Robbery causing death and robbery causing injury carry different sentences.'

issues.concern: This absolute claim holds only for the negative-copula use (sense 1). The tag-question じゃない (sense 2) does follow i-adjectives and verbs directly, as in the entry's own examples いいじゃない！ and 美味しかったじゃない. A learner could take the two as contradictory.
issues.suggestion: Limit the claim to negation, e.g. 'As a negative, it cannot attach directly to i-adjectives or verbs… (the tag-question use in sense 2 can follow them: いいじゃない, 行くじゃない).'

issues.concern: False absolute. 毬栗 alone can mean the haircut; dictionaries list it as a short form of 毬栗頭. It does not always need 頭 or 刈り.
issues.suggestion: Say the haircut sense is usually expressed with 頭(あたま) or 刈(か)り, as in 毬栗頭 or 毬栗刈り, though 毬栗 alone can also mean it.

issues.concern: In Japanese, a recording device is レコーダー (ボイスレコーダー, ICレコーダー), not リコーダー. リコーダー refers only to the musical instrument, so the claimed homonymy is false.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 'Do not confuse with レコーダー (recording device, e.g. ボイスレコーダー, ICレコーダー); the instrument is リコーダー, while recording devices are レコーダー.'

issues.concern: ライブハウス is wasei-eigo. 'Live house' is not natural English, so learners may wrongly think it is the English term for a small live-music venue.
issues.suggestion: Backstage at the club (live music venue), the drummer was rehearsing.

issues.concern: 老木 is largely a neutral descriptive term for an aged tree, often used in matter-of-fact contexts such as felling decayed or dangerous old trees. It can even suggest declining vigor. Saying it inherently conveys respect rather than neutral observation overstates its connotation.
issues.suggestion: Say it is a somewhat written-style term that is often, but not necessarily, used with a sense of the tree's venerable age.

issues.concern: Overstated absolute. フェーズ is mainly business/technical, but it also appears in casual speech, e.g. 人生の新しいフェーズ or 今はそういうフェーズじゃない.
issues.suggestion: Soften to: 'Mainly a business/technical loanword, though increasingly heard in casual speech (e.g. 人生のフェーズ).'

issues.concern: Overstated. Standalone フード meaning 'food' is common in restaurant, café and bar contexts, e.g. menus divided into フード and ドリンク, or フードメニュー. The word is not almost always read as 'hood' when it stands alone.
issues.suggestion: Soften the claim, e.g.: 'In everyday conversation, フード by itself usually means "hood," though on menus and in the restaurant trade it commonly means "food" (as opposed to ドリンク).'

issues.concern: In Japan, 麻薬探知犬 (drug-detection dogs) are mainly run by customs (税関), not the police. Calling the term a subtype of 警察犬 is misleading for learners. Japanese police dogs mostly do tracking, scent identification, guarding and searching.
issues.suggestion: Describe 麻薬探知犬 as a drug-detection dog, typically used by customs (税関), and drop the claim that it is a role of 警察犬.

issues.concern: 動画カメラ is not an established Japanese term for a broader category, and phones are not normally called 動画カメラ. Presenting it as a standard, more general synonym that includes phones is likely misleading.
issues.suggestion: Remove this line, or replace it with an established related term such as カムコーダー (camcorder) or 業務用ビデオカメラ (professional video camera).

issues.concern: 写メ is short for 写メール, J-Phone's 2000 service name (later Vodafone/SoftBank), not directly for 写真メール. The same claim appears in definitions[0].explanation.
issues.suggestion: Say it is short for 写メール (しゃメール), J-Phone's photo-mail service name, itself a blend of 写真 and メール.

issues.concern: 非常用口 is not a standard term. The usual word for 'emergency exit' is 非常口(ひじょうぐち), and a learner would pick up a nonexistent form.
issues.suggestion: Replace with 非常用出口(ひじょうようでぐち): emergency exit, or drop the line and mention 非常口(ひじょうぐち) as the standard word.

issues.concern: False restriction. 非常用 is routinely used as a predicate with だ/です, e.g. この懐中電灯は非常用です ('This flashlight is for emergencies').
issues.suggestion: Remove the sentence, or say it is also used predicatively with だ/です (この水は非常用です).

issues.concern: ネックウォーマー is not wasei-eigo. 'Neck warmer' is an ordinary English term, so a learner would wrongly think it is not understood in English.
issues.suggestion: Say it is a loanword from English 'neck warmer'. If wanted, add that 'neck gaiter' and 'snood' are also used in English.

issues.concern: Rendering ベストスコアを更新する as 'update my golf best score' is unnatural English. In this context 更新 means beating or breaking a personal best, and the calque would teach learners a non-idiomatic expression.
issues.suggestion: I practice every week to beat my best golf score.

issues.concern: 上皇 is the standard abbreviation of 太上天皇; they name the same title. Saying 上皇 is 'distinguished from' 太上天皇 misrepresents the etymology.
issues.suggestion: State that 上皇 is a shortened form of 太上天皇(だいじょうてんのう), the full formal title.

issues.concern: The title was last conferred in 1817, on Emperor Kōkaku's abdication. He held it until his death in 1840, so it was not last 'used' in 1817.
issues.suggestion: Say the title was last conferred in 1817 (Emperor Kōkaku).

issues.concern: Here 御所 means an imperial residence. The Emperor Emeritus lives at the Sentō Imperial Residence in Akasaka, not the Imperial Palace (皇居), so the English gives a wrong location.
issues.suggestion: His Majesty the Emperor Emeritus currently lives in an imperial residence.

issues.concern: 打刻 predates time cards. Its original and still-current meaning is stamping or punching characters or numbers into a surface, such as metal (e.g. 車台番号の打刻). The time-card use is a later extension, so the note misstates the word's origin.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite as: 'Originally means stamping or engraving marks or numbers into a surface (e.g. metal); in workplaces it came to mean stamping a time card, and now any electronic time-recording action.'

issues.concern: 果たす is written with the same kanji 果, not a 'related' one. Its meaning is also not 'entirely different': both verbs centre on bringing something to its end. 果たす even has a parallel completive suffix use, as in 使い果たす 'to use up completely'.
issues.suggestion: Intransitive. Its transitive counterpart is 果(は)たす (to accomplish, to fulfill, to carry through to the end), written with the same kanji; as a suffix it also means 'to do completely' (e.g. 使(つか)い果(は)たす, to use up).

issues.concern: The etymology is wrong. 揺り is the continuative form of 揺る (ゆる, to shake), as in 揺り籠 and 揺り返し. It does not come from 揺する, whose continuative form is 揺すり.
issues.suggestion: Compound of 揺(ゆ)る (to shake; cf. 揺する) + 起(お)こす (to wake).

issues.concern: This collocation is unnatural. The object of 揺り起こす is the person being woken, not the shoulder; the natural phrasing is 肩を揺すって起こす. The collocation also contradicts the note's own transitivity statement.
issues.suggestion: Replace with 肩(かた)を揺(ゆ)すって起(お)こす: to shake someone by the shoulder to wake them, or remove the line.

issues.concern: The claim is overstated. Animals can be shaken awake, and the verb is also used figuratively, e.g. 記憶を揺り起こす or 眠っていた感情を揺り起こす.
issues.suggestion: The object is usually a sleeping person (or animal); it can also be used figuratively for stirring up dormant memories or feelings.

issues.concern: The standard reading of 軽々しい is かるがるしい; かろがろしい is an archaic/rare variant. It is also not 'unrelated' to かるがる, since both come from the same root 軽い.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite as: 軽々(かるがる)しい looks similar but means 'thoughtless, rash, careless'. It is a negative adjective, so don't confuse it with the adverb 軽々と.

issues.concern: 易々と means 'very easily, readily'. It often appears in critical contexts (e.g. やすやすと騙される, 'to be fooled all too easily'), but it does not suggest that a task was 'deceptively easy'.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite as: 易々(やすやす)と: very easily, readily — often used critically of something that happened too easily (e.g. being fooled, letting an opponent through).

issues.concern: せんじょう is written with the same kanji 戦場 as いくさば, not with different kanji.
issues.suggestion: Change to: '戦場(いくさば): battlefield (the same kanji are more commonly read せんじょう)'.

issues.concern: ホットスポットがある uses the full word, so calling it a shortening of ホットスポット is confused and misleading. The real point is that ホットスポット alone can mean a Wi-Fi hotspot when context makes it clear.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase: 'In context, ホットスポット alone can refer to a Wi-Fi hotspot, e.g. ここにホットスポットがある (there's a Wi-Fi hotspot here).'

issues.concern: Under 年俸制 (annual salary system), pay is set as an annual amount, but it is not paid as a single annual total. Japan's Labor Standards Act requires wages to be paid at least once a month, so the annual sum is paid in monthly installments.
issues.suggestion: - 年俸制(ねんぽうせい): annual salary system — pay is set as an annual amount (usually paid out in monthly installments)

issues.concern: The 'almost always' restriction is false. 晴雨兼用 is also common as a predicate with だ/です and directly prefixed to nouns without の. The entry itself shows both: example 1 (晴雨兼用だ) and the collocation 晴雨兼用傘.
issues.suggestion: Say it is commonly used as a noun modifier with の, and also used predicatively (晴雨兼用だ) and directly prefixed to nouns (晴雨兼用傘).

issues.concern: The etymology is wrong. 伝線 has never meant 'transmission line'; dictionaries record only the stocking-run sense. The name comes from the kanji 伝 (travel along) + 線 (line), describing how the snag spreads, not from an earlier word with another meaning.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite as: 'From 伝 (to travel/spread along) + 線 (line), describing the way a tiny snag in stockings rapidly spreads along a vertical line of thread.'

issues.concern: 緑黄色野菜 means carotene-rich 'green and yellow vegetables' such as carrots, pumpkin and spinach, not just green vegetables. 'Green vegetable smoothie' narrows the meaning and suggests a green smoothie.
issues.suggestion: I try to drink a smoothie made with green and yellow vegetables every morning.

issues.concern: 'legal obligation' names the resulting state (法的義務), not the act of making something obligatory. 義務化 means 'making mandatory' and covers institutional requirements as well as legal ones.
issues.suggestion: making (something) mandatory; imposing an obligation

issues.concern: 垂れ下がる describes a flexible object hanging down from a point, not liquid trickling or flowing. 汗が垂れ下がる is not a natural collocation, and 'sweat trickles down' is not a meaning of this verb. The natural expressions are 汗が垂れる or 汗が流れる.
issues.suggestion: Remove this collocation, or replace it with a natural one such as 'カーテンが垂れ下がる: a curtain hangs down'.

issues.concern: False restriction. ホイール is also commonly used outside vehicles, e.g. マウスホイール (scroll wheel on a computer mouse) and ホイールローダー (wheel loader).
issues.suggestion: Soften the claim: 'In Japanese, ホイール most often refers to the rigid wheel structure (hub + rim) of cars, motorcycles, and bicycles, though it also appears in loanword compounds such as マウスホイール (mouse scroll wheel).'

issues.concern: 醤油顔 describes facial features, such as a shallow profile, single eyelids and a narrow face. It does not describe body type, so 'slim build' is wrong.
issues.suggestion: Change 'slim build' to 'narrow face' or 'shallow facial contours'.

issues.concern: 'Atmosphere' for a person's 雰囲気 is a Japanese calque and sounds unnatural in English. Learners may copy it.
issues.suggestion: She has delicate features, and her cool, refreshing air is attractive.

issues.concern: The note limits 近代的 to the historical period (post-Meiji to mid-20th century). In fact 近代的 is widely used today to mean 'modernized, up-to-date, westernized' (e.g. 近代的な設備, 近代的なビル). Only the noun 近代 names that historical era.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase as: 近代的(きんだいてき): modern, modernized — contrasts with feudal or premodern; the related noun 近代 refers to the Meiji-to-WWII era.

issues.concern: 込み does not come after particles. In 税・送料込で and 込みの値段, the particle follows 込み. The note misstates the word order.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite as: 'Used both as a bound suffix (税込) and as a word followed by particles such as で or の (送料込みで, 込みの値段).'

issues.concern: 'sat there' adds a posture the Japanese never mentions; the sentence only says he stayed sullenly silent and said nothing.
issues.suggestion: He stayed sullenly silent and said nothing.

issues.concern: The gloss for カチンとくる reverses the direction. 'To get a rise out of' someone means to provoke them into reacting. カチンとくる describes the person who is irritated, not the provoker.
issues.suggestion: Gloss it as 'to be irked; to get one's hackles up; to be rubbed the wrong way' and drop 'to get a rise out of'.

issues.concern: "Wonderfully" adds a degree and positive judgment that the neutral Japanese このゼリーはぷるぷるしている does not contain.
issues.suggestion: This jelly is nice and jiggly. / This jelly is jiggly.

issues.concern: '戦時中下で' is not a valid Japanese expression. The correct collocation for 'under wartime conditions' is 戦時下で, built on 戦時 rather than 戦時中.
issues.suggestion: Replace with '- 戦時下(せんじか)で: under wartime conditions' or remove the line.

issues.concern: The Portuguese source term is misspelled. The correct form is 'futebol de salão', not 'futbol de salão'.
issues.suggestion: Change to 'Loanword from Portuguese futebol de salão / Spanish fútbol sala.'

issues.concern: Overstated absolute. フットボール is used for soccer in Japanese, especially in names and soccer media: Jリーグ's official name is 日本プロサッカーリーグ, but the JFL is 日本フットボールリーグ, and there are soccer outlets such as フットボールチャンネル. Soccer is usually, not always, called サッカー.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 'In everyday Japanese, soccer is usually called サッカー, though フットボール does refer to soccer in some names and soccer media (e.g. 日本フットボールリーグ).'

issues.concern: コストパフォーマンス is usually classed as wasei-eigo (Japanese-coined English). 'Cost performance' is not a normal English expression for 'value for money', so calling it simply a loanword from English may mislead learners into using it in English.
issues.suggestion: Loanword built from English elements (often classed as wasei-eigo); in English, 'value for money' or 'cost-effectiveness' is used instead.

issues.concern: ヨガウェア is not wasei-eigo. 'Yoga wear' is a common English term in its own right, and the entry's own gloss uses it, so labelling it a Japanese-made English expression is a false etymology claim.
issues.suggestion: Describe it as a loanword from English 'yoga wear' and remove the wasei-eigo claim.

issues.concern: デフレ is not a colloquial form. It is the standard neutral term used in newspapers, government and Bank of Japan documents, and economic writing (e.g. デフレ脱却). Calling it colloquial could lead learners to avoid it in formal contexts.
issues.suggestion: - デフレ: deflation — clipped form, standard in both everyday and formal/news usage and much more common

issues.concern: 内 (ない) here is a bound suffix meaning 'within X' (アプリ内, ゲーム内); it does not stand alone. When アプリ内課金 is shortened in actual Japanese usage, it becomes 課金, not 内課金. Standalone 内課金 is not an established clipping. The entry's own explanation also says the word almost always appears inside アプリ内課金.
issues.suggestion: Drop the clipping claim. Describe 内課金 as the second element of compounds such as アプリ内課金 and ゲーム内課金, and note that the everyday short form is 課金.

issues.concern: 以前 is common in everyday speech (e.g. 以前ここに住んでいた), not limited to a formal written register. It is only somewhat more formal than 前に.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 'previously; formerly — somewhat more formal than 前に; used in both speech and writing'.

issues.concern: The claim that 下を向く has 'no emotional reading' is false. 下を向く is commonly used figuratively for dejection or shame, e.g. 下を向くな ('don't lose heart') and 下を向いてばかりいる.
issues.suggestion: Say that 下を向く is the plain physical description, but that it is also often used figuratively for discouragement or shame.

issues.concern: 'predictably' is added. The Japanese 結局…というオチがついた says only that the matter ended with the reveal that the wallet had been left at home. It does not say the outcome was predictable.
issues.suggestion: In the end, it turned out I'd left my wallet at home.

issues.concern: 'to wind up predictably' misstates the meaning. オチがつく means a story or matter reaches its punchline or conclusion, often with a twist. Predictability is not part of the meaning, and the twist is often unexpected.
issues.suggestion: to come to a punchline; to be wrapped up (with a twist); to find a fitting end

issues.concern: The phrase is listed as a common collocation of オチがつく, but it does not contain the headword and is not an established expression.
issues.suggestion: Remove this line or replace it with a real collocation, e.g. 話にオチがつく.

issues.concern: 習い慣れた道 is not a natural collocation, since a road is not something one learns (習う). The natural form is 通い慣れた道 or 歩き慣れた道. Presenting it as a typical attributive use, also in example 0, would mislead learners.
issues.suggestion: Replace 習い慣れた道 with a skill-related noun, e.g. 習い慣れた手順 or 習い慣れた仕事. Revise example 0 to match.

issues.concern: The notes propose the honorific verb 仰る ('to say') as a possible source of the interjection. There is no such link. おっしゃ is a phonetic variant of よっしゃ, which comes from よし. The resemblance to おっしゃる is coincidental.
issues.suggestion: Say that おっしゃ is a variant of よっしゃ (from よし), and drop the reference to 仰る.

issues.concern: The claim that どっちでも構わない is 'often masculine' is unfounded. 構わない is gender-neutral and used by all speakers. It reads as slightly more formal or stiff than いい, not as masculine.
issues.suggestion: Drop 'often masculine'; describe it as 'either is fine; slightly more formal/firm than どっちでもいい'.

issues.concern: なおさら is not limited to positive cases. It is used just as often in negative escalation, e.g. 大人でも難しいのだから、子供ならなおさら無理だ. Saying it applies to positive cases falsely restricts its use.
issues.suggestion: Describe なおさら as 'all the more; even more so', usable in both positive and negative contexts, often in the pattern 〜ならなおさら.

issues.concern: 月夜 means the night itself, not the light, so 月夜に照らされる ('to be lit by the moonlight') is not a natural collocation. The notes' own similar-words section says 月明かり is the word for the light itself, which contradicts this line.
issues.suggestion: Replace with a natural collocation such as 月明かりに照らされる, or with 月夜の散歩 ('a moonlit walk').

issues.concern: The formality label 'neutral' conflicts with the notes, which describe the word as somewhat formal or written.
issues.suggestion: Change formality to 'formal', or soften the note if 'neutral' is intended.

issues.concern: The absolute 'never use 歌う' is false. 鳴く is the standard verb, but 歌う is used for insects in poetic or personified writing (e.g. 虫たちが歌う).
issues.suggestion: Soften the claim: 'The verb 鳴(な)く is the standard word for the sound; 歌(うた)う appears only in poetic or personified contexts.'

issues.concern: In English, 'moonflower' normally means Ipomoea alba, which the entry's own notes assign to 夜顔. Attaching 'moonflower' to Lagenaria siceraria contradicts the notes and misleads learners; the English name for that plant is bottle gourd or calabash.
issues.suggestion: bottle gourd plant; calabash (Lagenaria siceraria). If 'moonflower' is kept, mark it as a separate colloquial use referring to Ipomoea alba.

issues.concern: Calystegia japonica is Japanese bindweed (ヒルガオ). 'Field bindweed' is a different plant, Convolvulus arvensis, which is セイヨウヒルガオ in Japanese. The gloss gives the wrong common name for the species.
issues.suggestion: Japanese bindweed (Calystegia japonica); related Calystegia species

issues.concern: 'Field bindweed' is Convolvulus arvensis (セイヨウヒルガオ), not 昼顔 (Calystegia japonica).
issues.suggestion: bindweed; Japanese bindweed

issues.concern: 'Moonflower' (Ipomoea alba) is ヨルガオ, a morning-glory relative. 夕顔 is properly the bottle gourd, as the entry's own SIMILAR WORDS line says. The two lines contradict each other.
issues.suggestion: Forms a set with 朝顔(あさがお) (morning glory) and 夕顔(ゆうがお) (bottle gourd).

issues.concern: The English drops 茶漉しで ('with a tea strainer'). That phrase is the headword itself, so the learner can't see which part of the sentence the headword maps to.
issues.suggestion: I strained the tea with a tea strainer so no leaves would get into the cup.

issues.concern: Calling ドアホン wasei-eigo is doubtful. "Door phone" (also "doorphone") is an established English term for an entrance intercom, so ドアホン is more likely an ordinary loanword from English.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: From English "door phone."

issues.concern: Wrong reading for 毛糸: it is けいと, so アクリル毛糸 is read あくりるけいと. The given 毛(げ)糸(いと) would be read 'げいと', which is incorrect; 毛糸 takes no rendaku here.
issues.suggestion: - アクリル毛糸(けいと): acrylic yarn

issues.concern: The 'almost exclusively' restriction is false. とろみ is also commonly used outside cooking, for example for hot-spring water (とろみのある湯) and for cosmetics such as lotions (とろみのある化粧水).
issues.suggestion: Used mainly for the thickness of liquids in cooking; also for other viscous liquids such as hot-spring water and cosmetics, and increasingly for thickened drinks in care for the elderly to prevent choking.

issues.concern: The etymology is doubtful. とろみ is normally explained as the root とろ (as in とろい, とろり, とろとろ) plus the noun suffix -み. It does not come from a verb, and とろりとする is an adverb plus する, not a verb in its own right.
issues.suggestion: Formed from とろ (as in とろり, とろとろ) + the noun-forming suffix -み.

issues.concern: Zoological and scientific writing uses ヒキガエル (e.g. アズマヒキガエル, ニホンヒキガエル), not ガマ. ガマ is the colloquial or traditional name. This claim also contradicts the note's own statement that ヒキガエル is 'more standard'.
issues.suggestion: Say that the katakana ガマ is common in casual and traditional contexts, while ヒキガエル is the standard term in zoology and nature writing.

issues.concern: The Japanese giant salamander is not the world's largest amphibian. The Chinese giant salamander (Andrias davidianus / A. sligoi) is larger; the Japanese species is one of the largest.
issues.suggestion: Change to "...is one of the world's largest amphibians and a famous protected species."

issues.concern: The explanation calls the giant salamander a "national treasure" (国宝), which is a different legal category. Its actual designation is Special Natural Monument (特別天然記念物), as example 2 states.
issues.suggestion: Change to "The Japanese giant salamander is designated a Special Natural Monument."

issues.concern: The お in お玉 is an honorific/beautifying prefix, not a diminutive meaning 'little'. 玉 means 'ball/sphere', so お玉杓子 is literally 'ball-shaped ladle'. The 'little' reading gives a false etymology.
issues.suggestion: Literally お玉杓子(おたまじゃくし), a round ladle (honorific お + 玉 'ball' + 杓子 'ladle'), which the tadpole's shape resembles.

issues.concern: 肥やす is not the causative form of 肥える; it is its lexical transitive counterpart. The causative of 肥える is 肥えさせる. Calling it causative misleads learners about how it is formed.
issues.suggestion: Transitive counterpart of 肥(こ)える (to grow fat; for soil to become rich).

issues.concern: The claim is overstated. 何百 often appears without a counter (何百もの本, 何百という人), without も (何百万円かかる, 何百人いるの？), and in compounds like 何百万. The entry's own collocation 何百万円 and its question example contradict it.
issues.suggestion: Soften to: "Usually appears with a counter, and often with も or もの, to mean 'hundreds of...'"

issues.concern: 捕まる is read つかまる, not とまる. It is also the intransitive pair of 捕まえる, not of 捕る.
issues.suggestion: Change to: No direct intransitive pair; compare 捕(つか)まる (to be caught), the intransitive counterpart of 捕(つか)まえる.

issues.concern: 犯人を捕る is not a standard collocation. Criminals are normally caught with 捕まえる or 捕らえる.
issues.suggestion: Replace with 犯人(はんにん)を捕(つか)まえる／捕(と)らえる, or drop this collocation.

issues.concern: 三貫 is read さんかん, not さんがん. The counter 貫 does not undergo rendaku after 三.
issues.suggestion: Change 三(さん)貫(がん) to 三(さん)貫(かん); only 一 changes (いっかん).

issues.concern: The standard etymology says the bumpy tip of the pepper resembles a lion's head or face (獅子頭), not a lion's mane. Saying 'mane' also contradicts the note's own 'lion's-head pepper'.
issues.suggestion: Change to: named because the bumpy tip resembles the head of a lion (獅子).

issues.concern: The etymology is likely wrong. ぼっくり is usually traced to ふぐり (scrotum), via まつふぐり → まつぼくり → まつぼっくり. It is not an independent older word for a small round shape.
issues.suggestion: Say that ぼっくり is generally explained as a sound change from ふぐり (scrotum), from the earlier form 松ふぐり (まつふぐり).

issues.concern: This gets the direction wrong. American all-purpose flour (about 10–12% protein) has more protein than 中力粉 (about 8–10.5%), not less. So it is closer to a blend of 中力粉 and 強力粉, not 薄力粉 and 中力粉.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: Note that Japanese 中力粉(ちゅうりきこ) is closer in protein content to British "plain flour" than to American all-purpose flour, which is somewhat higher in protein, between 中力粉(ちゅうりきこ) and 強力粉(きょうりきこ).

issues.concern: The TV series 水戸黄門 is not set in Mito. Its protagonist is the retired lord of Mito (Tokugawa Mitsukuni), but the show follows his travels through provinces all over Japan.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase as: '...and its retired lord Tokugawa Mitsukuni is the hero of the long-running TV series 水戸黄門(みとこうもん), which follows his travels around Japan.'

issues.concern: The proverb いずれアヤメか杜若 compares only two flowers, アヤメ and 杜若. The note wrongly says it refers to three, which brings in 花菖蒲 by implication.
issues.suggestion: Say that the proverb means both flowers are equally beautiful and it is hard to choose between them (used of two equally attractive people or things).

issues.concern: Standard dictionaries such as Daijirin and Kōjien treat 小焼け in 夕焼け小焼け as a word added only for rhythm, to echo 夕焼け. It has no established meaning of its own. Stating it as 'the softer red glow that follows 夕焼け' presents a folk interpretation as fact.
issues.suggestion: Gloss it as a rhythmic echo of 夕焼け, e.g. 'rhythmic echo of 夕焼け (in 夕焼けこやけ)', and say in the explanation that it has little independent meaning.

issues.concern: 噂 is not narrower than 都市伝説. It covers any rumor, gossip or hearsay, and an urban legend is essentially a kind of 噂. The difference is that 噂 lacks the narrative and folkloric character, not that its scope is narrower.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'narrower' with something like: 'rumor; gossip — general hearsay about people or events, without the narrative, folklore-like character of 都市伝説'.

issues.concern: くたびれる is not literary. It is common in everyday, casual speech (e.g. 'あー、くたびれた'), so calling it literary or old-fashioned misleads learners about its register. The same claim appears in definitions[0].explanation.
issues.suggestion: Describe くたびれる as colloquial/conversational, with a nuance of being worn down or drained, rather than literary or old-fashioned.

issues.concern: ごろん is not limited to deliberate acts. It also describes involuntary toppling and inanimate objects rolling (e.g. 石がごろんと転がる). The entry's own pattern ごろんと倒れる contradicts 'deliberate'.
issues.suggestion: Mimetic adverb for a single act of flopping down, rolling over, or (of a heavy object) rolling or toppling once.

issues.concern: Overstated restriction. 洋楽器 is often used on its own without any explicit contrast with 和楽器, as in music-shop categories and school equipment. The entry's own examples 0 and 2 show this.
issues.suggestion: Soften to: 'Often used in contrast with 和楽器(わがっき) (Japanese instruments).'

issues.concern: The claim is misleading. 過去最高の and 観測史上最も〜 are not softer conversational alternatives to 記録的. They are more precise, and 観測史上 is itself formal news and meteorological language, not conversational hedging.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase, e.g.: 'For more precise statements, news reports also use 過去最高の (highest ever) or 観測史上最も〜 (the most since records began).'

issues.concern: The wild population in Japan did not end in 2003. The last five wild birds were captured in 1981, which ended the wild population. 2003 is when Kin, the last Japan-born ibis, died in captivity.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite to say the wild population ended in 1981, when the last wild birds were captured, and the last Japan-born bird died in captivity in 2003.

issues.concern: In choral terminology, 四部 in 混声四部(合唱) is normally read しぶ, so こんせいしぶがっしょう. The reading よんぶ would mislead learners.
issues.suggestion: Change to 混声(こんせい)四部(しぶ): mixed four-part (SATB)

issues.concern: The 風 in 風疹 most likely comes from the Chinese-medicine idea of 'wind' (風) as a cause of disease, or from the rash coming and going quickly like wind. Saying it suggests 'the disease's spread' appears to be a folk explanation.
issues.suggestion: Explain 風 as 'wind' in the traditional medical sense of a pathogenic influence, e.g. 'Compound of 風(ふう) (wind, in the traditional medical sense of a disease-causing influence) + 疹(しん) (rash).'

issues.concern: 'Welsh onion' is the standard English name for 葱 (Allium fistulosum), not wakegi. Wakegi is a hybrid of the Welsh onion and the shallot, so this gloss names a different plant.
issues.suggestion: Remove 'Welsh onion': 'wakegi; bunching onion (Allium × wakegi), a Welsh onion–shallot hybrid'

issues.concern: The 'almost exclusively' restriction is overstated. The compound 最寄り駅 is at least as common as 最寄りの駅, and the notes themselves list it. Colloquially, 最寄り also stands alone as a noun meaning 'one's nearest station'.
issues.suggestion: Say it is mostly used attributively, either as 最寄りの + noun or in compounds such as 最寄り駅.

issues.concern: The note overstates ミリ as a millimeter-only word. Standalone ミリ is also very commonly used colloquially for milliliters (e.g., 500ミリのペットボトル, ジュース350ミリ), so learners would be misled into thinking the full compound is required.
issues.suggestion: Say that ミリ alone usually means millimeter but is also commonly used for milliliter when context makes it clear (e.g., drink volumes like 500ミリ), while other units generally use the full compound.

issues.concern: 体育会系 is not a synonym for 運動部. It is a descriptive term for the culture, personality or style associated with athletic clubs, as the SIMILAR WORDS section itself says. It does not name the club, so 体育会系に入っている is not used for 運動部に入っている.
issues.suggestion: Say that 体育会系 (often paired with 文化系) describes the athletic-club category, style or culture, such as 体育会系の部活 or 体育会系の人, rather than serving as another word for 運動部.

issues.concern: The Japanese asks whether the person has bowel movements at all. 'Regular' is not in the sentence and adds the idea of regularity.
issues.suggestion: Have you been having bowel movements?

issues.concern: The Japanese says only 'a bookmark made from pressed flowers'. It does not say the grandmother made it, so 'she had made' adds an agent.
issues.suggestion: My grandmother carefully kept a bookmark made from pressed flowers.

issues.concern: The note presents 除け as the only kanji spelling. 避け is also used (e.g. 日避け, 雨避け, 風避け), and the notes and definition themselves derive the word from 避ける.
issues.suggestion: Say that 除け is the most common kanji spelling (e.g. 虫除け, 魔除け), and that 避け is also used (e.g. 日避け, 風避け).

issues.concern: In English, 'suspended from school' implies a disciplinary punishment. Here the absence is a mandatory health-related exclusion, so a learner may take the wrong sense.
issues.suggestion: I was barred from attending school because of the flu. / I had to stay home from school because of the flu.

issues.concern: 'Spring spring tides' reads like a typo, and learners may not see that it means spring tides (大潮) occurring in springtime.
issues.suggestion: The spring tides in springtime are the best time for tide pool exploration.

issues.concern: The claim that ボクサー refers only to the athlete is false. The standalone word is also used for the dog breed and sometimes for boxer briefs. The notes themselves contradict this claim further down.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "Most often refers to the athlete; it can also mean the dog breed or men's boxer underwear, which is usually clear from context (see below)."

issues.concern: False absolute. 包丁さばき is a neutral noun and often appears with negative modifiers (包丁さばきが下手, ぎこちない包丁さばき, 危なっかしい包丁さばき). Praise is common, but the word itself is not always positive.
issues.suggestion: Say it is neutral but frequently used in praise, e.g. 'Neutral in itself, but very often used to praise someone's cutting skill; can also be criticized (包丁さばきが下手, ぎこちない包丁さばき).'

issues.concern: 躱す and 交わす are written with different kanji, so they are not homographs in kanji. They are homophones that look identical only when written in kana.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 'かわす (交(か)わす): a homophone written with different kanji (identical in kana), meaning "to exchange (words, glances)" — different verb'

issues.concern: The transitive counterpart of 擦(す)れる is 擦(す)る / 摩(す)る (as in マッチを擦る), not 擦(こす)る. 擦(こす)る pairs with 擦(こす)れる.
issues.suggestion: State that the transitive counterpart is 擦(す)る (to rub, strike), and note that 擦(こす)る is the transitive partner of 擦(こす)れる.

issues.concern: This line gives the wrong transitive pair: すれる pairs with する, not こする.
issues.suggestion: Change to: transitive pair: 〜を擦(す)る (to rub, strike)

issues.concern: The reading for 水生植物 is wrong. 水生 is read すいせい, not みず + せい, so the ruby as written gives the incorrect みずせいしょくぶつ.
issues.suggestion: Write it as 水生(すいせい)植物(しょくぶつ), read すいせいしょくぶつ.

issues.concern: 先入観 means a preconception: an idea formed in advance about anything. It is not restricted to individual cases and is often used about groups (e.g. 外国人に対する先入観). The claimed restriction is false.
issues.suggestion: - 先入観(せんにゅうかん): preconception — an idea formed in advance, before actual experience; focuses on prior assumption rather than a socially shared image

issues.concern: This misstates the constitutional triggers. Under Article 70, the cabinet resigns en masse when the Diet first convenes after any general election, whatever the result. Under Article 69, it does so after a no-confidence vote unless the lower house is dissolved. It also resigns when the PM post becomes vacant. An election loss is not itself the constitutional trigger.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase to: 'a constitutional event that occurs, e.g., after a no-confidence vote, when the prime minister's post becomes vacant, or when the Diet first convenes after a general election; it can also follow a major political setback.'

issues.concern: In Japan, 粽 usually means a sweet rice-cake or dumpling wrapped in bamboo or sasa leaves, shaped as a long cone. The description fits Chinese zongzi instead. Niigata's own chimaki, the counterpart to sasa dango, is also not savory.
issues.suggestion: 粽(ちまき): rice cake or dumpling wrapped in bamboo or sasa leaves, often elongated and eaten at Children's Day; Chinese-style zongzi versions are pyramidal and often savory

issues.concern: 両輪を担う usually has both parties as its subject (e.g. 国と地方が両輪を担う), meaning they serve together as the two pillars. Glossing it as taking on just one of the two roles misreads 両輪 ('both wheels').
issues.suggestion: Gloss as 'to serve (together) as the two pillars/essential parts'; for one party, use 両輪の一つを担う.

issues.concern: むちゃくちゃ (無茶苦茶, from 無茶) is not a casual variant of めちゃくちゃ. It is a standard word in its own right and is generally considered the source form. Both words are equally colloquial.
issues.suggestion: Say instead: 'Closely related to めちゃくちゃ (滅茶苦茶) and largely interchangeable with it; both are colloquial.'

issues.concern: The formal reading of the degree title 理学博士 is りがくはくし. はかせ is a common colloquial reading, but a learner may take it as the standard reading for the degree.
issues.suggestion: Give the reading as 理学(りがく)博士(はくし), optionally noting that はかせ is also heard colloquially.

issues.concern: No い is dropped. The 連用形 (stem) of 失くす is 失くし, and 物 attaches to it directly, as in 落とし物 and 忘れ物.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 'Formed from the stem (連用形) of 失(な)くす, 失くし, plus 物(もの).'

issues.concern: 紙の両側 most naturally means the two edges of the paper, not front and back. 'Print on both sides' (double-sided) is 両面に印刷, so the example teaches a mismatched pairing.
issues.suggestion: Use 紙の両面に印刷してください for double-sided printing, or replace the example with a spatial one such as 机の両側に椅子を置く.

issues.concern: The explanation lists 'a piece of paper' as a typical use. The front and back of paper are 両面, not 両側, so learners may misuse the word.
issues.suggestion: Remove 'a piece of paper' from the explanation or replace it with something like 'a river' or 'a gate'.

issues.concern: 両側通行 is not a standard term for 'two-way traffic', which is usually 対面通行 or 双方向通行. The collocation is doubtful.
issues.suggestion: Replace it with a common collocation such as 川の両側 or 両側から挟む.

issues.concern: Standalone 式場 is very commonly used for funerals (e.g. 通夜・告別式の案内: 式場：○○会館) and for school ceremonies (卒業式の式場). Compounds are not normally required for these, and the claim also contradicts the explanation's 'most often weddings or funerals'.
issues.suggestion: Say that standalone 式場 refers to the venue of whatever ceremony the context implies, often a wedding but frequently a funeral or school ceremony.

issues.concern: "News of his passing" normally means news of his death in English. 合格 means passing an exam, so the translation suggests the opposite situation.
issues.suggestion: The whole family was overjoyed at the news that he had passed the exam.

issues.concern: すみません is polite (the ます-form of すむ), the standard everyday polite apology. It is not casual; the casual forms are ごめん and ごめんなさい.
issues.suggestion: Describe すみません as a common everyday polite apology phrase, and give ごめん / ごめんなさい as the casual forms if a casual contrast is wanted.

issues.concern: 真冬 is read まふゆ (kun'yomi ま), not しん, so this example does not illustrate the headword 真(しん). The entry's own notes list 真冬 under the ま reading, which makes it contradict itself and suggests to learners that 真冬 uses しん.
issues.suggestion: Replace with a compound that uses しん, e.g. 真相(しんそう)が明らかになった。'The truth came to light.' or 彼の真価が問われる。'His true worth is being tested.'

issues.concern: 他生 is not just another spelling of 多生. It is a separate word meaning 'another life (past or future)', not 'many lives'. The two are interchangeable only in the proverb 袖振り合うも多生/他生の縁.
issues.suggestion: Say that the proverb is also written 他生の縁, where 他生 means 'another (past or future) life', rather than calling it a variant spelling with the same meaning.

issues.concern: 美味しい has no reading びみしい. It is read おいしい (ateji). 美味 alone is read びみ, a noun / na-adjective meaning 'deliciousness; delicious'. As written, the note teaches a nonexistent word and wrongly calls おいしい merely 'the more common form'.
issues.suggestion: Replace with '- 美味(びみ): delicious taste; deliciousness (formal; cf. 美味(おい)しい, read おいしい)'.

issues.concern: "one's standard order" and the explanation's claim that お決まり refers to a customer's regular order at restaurants appear to misread お決まりですか. That phrase is the honorific form of 決まる ("Have you decided?"), not a noun meaning a regular order; a regular order is usually いつもの.
issues.suggestion: Drop "one's standard order" from the gloss and the explanation. Note that お決まりですか is the honorific お+決まり(verb stem)+です of 決まる, not the noun "the usual".

issues.concern: The standard reading of 多角形 is たかくけい. たかっけい is a colloquial variant. Giving only the variant contradicts the entry's own claim that the く form is standard (as with ろっかくけい).
issues.suggestion: Change to 多角形(たかくけい): polygon (general)

issues.concern: 'Highball' means spirits mixed with a larger amount of a cold mixer, usually soda. In Japan, ハイボール specifically means whisky and soda. 'Hot-water highball' is not established English and may confuse learners about what 湯割り is.
issues.suggestion: Drop 'hot-water highball'; use '(spirits) cut with hot water; (shochu) with hot water'

issues.concern: 'Hot-water highball' is not a natural English term and wrongly suggests a soda-based highball.
issues.suggestion: On a cold night, a drink cut with hot water warms you up.

issues.concern: 愚痴 is not limited to life or circumstances in general. People very commonly gripe about a specific person, as in 上司の愚痴 or 夫の愚痴. What sets it apart is that the griping is aired to a third party rather than addressed to the target.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase: '愚痴(ぐち): griping — grumbling to others about one's situation or about someone, rather than addressing a grievance to the person directly'

issues.concern: Overstated restriction. Bare 子息 without ご is common in written and journalistic Japanese, e.g. 政治家の子息 and 良家の子息.
issues.suggestion: Say it 'often' appears with ご in direct polite address, and that bare 子息 is common in writing about third parties.

issues.concern: The gloss 'to introduce one's son' conflicts with the rule that ご子息 never refers to one's own son. ご子息を紹介する means introducing someone else's son.
issues.suggestion: Gloss as 'to introduce (someone's) son', e.g. 社長のご子息を紹介する.

issues.concern: ひとり is the standard reading of 一人 in general, not an irregularity peculiar to this compound. 一人 is a jukujikun word read ひとり on its own as well, so the claim misleads learners. The sentence also contains a stray brace.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite as: 'The reading ひとり is the usual (jukujikun) reading of 一人, as in the standalone word.'

issues.concern: The standard idiom for gradual recovery from illness is 薄紙(うすがみ)を剥ぐように ('like peeling off thin paper'), not 薄皮をはぐように. 薄皮 here is a common misuse, so presenting it as the common expression would mislead learners. Example 2 has the same problem.
issues.suggestion: Change to 薄紙(うすがみ)をはぐように — 'like peeling away thin sheets of paper' — and note that 薄皮をはぐように is a common error. Remove or revise example 2 to match.

issues.concern: 'eat mizutaki refreshingly' is unidiomatic English for さっぱりと食べる and could teach learners a wrong collocation.
issues.suggestion: It's standard to eat mizutaki with ponzu and condiments for a light, refreshing taste.

issues.concern: The explanation lists 五月人形 as a festival name. It is not: 五月人形 are the warrior dolls displayed for Boys' Day (端午の節句/こどもの日).
issues.suggestion: Rephrase as: 'appears in historical contexts, in Boys' Day decorations (武者人形 among the 五月人形), and in set expressions such as 武者震い.'

issues.concern: Wrong kanji and pairing. ついやす is written 費やす, not 潰やす, so it is not presented as a kanji-sharing transitive partner of 潰える. Also, 時間を潰す ('kill time') is read つぶす, not ついやす.
issues.suggestion: Delete this claim, or say that 潰える has no common transitive counterpart in modern Japanese. If 費やす is mentioned, give its correct kanji, e.g. 時間(じかん)を費(つい)やす 'to spend time'.

issues.concern: 'Reserved for abstract things' is too absolute. 潰える also has a literal sense of physical things crumbling or collapsing, though it is rarer today. The notes' own example of military forces is not abstract either.
issues.suggestion: Say it is mainly used of abstract things such as dreams, plans and hopes, or of armies being routed.

issues.concern: 内地留学 standardly means domestic study leave: study or training at an institution within Japan, as opposed to studying abroad. Teachers sent to domestic universities are the typical case. It is not specifically a Hokkaido/Okinawa term for attending a mainland school.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 内地(ないち)留学(りゅうがく): domestic study leave (study/training at an institution within the country, as opposed to abroad)

issues.concern: The explanation says 等級 is used for judo/karate ranks. Martial-arts ranks are called 級 and 段 (e.g. 一級, 初段), not 等級, so this would mislead learners.
issues.suggestion: Remove 'judo/karate' from the explanation. A real use such as star magnitude (一等星, 等級) or sake/product grading could replace it.

issues.concern: The etymology is misstated. The satsuma originated in Japan (Nagashima, Kagoshima). It was named after Wenzhou because that region was famous for citrus, not because the variety was thought to come from there. The sentence also contradicts itself.
issues.suggestion: Named after Wenzhou (温州(うんしゅう)), a region in China famous for its citrus, although the variety itself originated in Japan (Kagoshima).

issues.concern: 土佐ポンカン is not a well-known regional variety; the famous Tosa citrus is 土佐文旦 (a pomelo), and the main ponkan regions are Kagoshima and Ehime. The collocation looks like a mix-up.
issues.suggestion: Replace it with an established ponkan name such as 吉田(よしだ)ポンカン or 太田(おおた)ポンカン, or drop the collocation.

issues.concern: Overclaim. Single-type rice miso (e.g., Shinshū-style) is the most widely sold miso in Japan, and blended miso is only a minority category. The stated reason is also unsupported.
issues.suggestion: Soften to: 'Blended miso is widely sold in supermarkets as a general-purpose miso.'

issues.concern: チゲ鍋 is a Japanese term, and redundant because チゲ already means 'stew'. In Japan it usually names the same kind of Japanese-style spicy nabe as キムチ鍋, not 'the original Korean stew'. The Korean original is kimchi-jjigae (キムチチゲ).
issues.suggestion: - チゲ鍋(なべ): Japanese term for a Korean-style spicy stew (from Korean jjigae), often used almost interchangeably with キムチ鍋

issues.concern: The note wrongly presents カメラマン as the everyday word for amateurs or hobbyists. カメラマン is the standard term for professional photographers and camera operators (press, studio, TV). A hobbyist is アマチュアカメラマン, 写真愛好家, or simply カメラ好き. The note sets up a false professional/amateur contrast.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 'カメラマン is the more common everyday word for a (usually professional) photographer or camera operator; a hobbyist is アマチュアカメラマン or 写真愛好家.'

issues.concern: 本宅勤務 is not an established collocation and does not mean 'working from one's main residence'. Working from home is 在宅勤務(ざいたくきんむ). Listing it as a common collocation would mislead learners.
issues.suggestion: Remove this line, or replace it with a genuine collocation such as 本宅(ほんたく)と別宅(べったく) (main residence and second home).

issues.concern: Japanese household utilities (公共料金) are conventionally electricity, gas and water, sometimes with telephone. Internet is not a standard member of this set, so 'four standard' with internet is misleading.
issues.suggestion: One of the standard household utility bills, along with electricity and water.

issues.concern: Strictly, 光熱費 covers lighting and heating fuel (electricity and gas, plus kerosene etc.). Water is usually counted separately, which is why the term 水道光熱費 exists.
issues.suggestion: - 光熱費(こうねつひ): utility costs for electricity and gas/fuel (with water: 水道光熱費)

issues.concern: Yin-yang reached Japan with Chinese learning (calendrical, divinatory and classical texts, later formalized as 陰陽道), not through Shinto, which is native and absorbed the idea rather than transmitting it. Naming Buddhism as the channel is also misleading.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase: 'Deeply rooted in Chinese cosmology; introduced to Japan with Chinese learning (around the 6th–7th centuries) and later blended into Shinto, Buddhist practice, and traditional medicine.'

issues.concern: 資格 means 'qualification/certification', not specifically 'license' (免許). The entry's own notes gloss 資格保持者 as 'certification holder' and list 免許保持者 separately as 'license holder', so this translation is inconsistent with them.
issues.suggestion: He holds a qualification. / He is a certified professional.

issues.concern: The claim that アウトソーシング has 'largely replaced' 外部委託 is likely overstated. 外部委託 and 業務委託 are still widely used in business, government and media alongside the loanword, as the entry's own SIMILAR WORDS section suggests.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase to: 'A business-world term used alongside native expressions like 外部委託(がいぶいたく).'

issues.concern: The claim that the お prefix is always included is false. 色直し (いろなおし) without お is a standard dictionary headword and appears in writing.
issues.suggestion: Say that the お prefix is almost always used in everyday speech, but that 色直し without お also exists.

issues.concern: The headword is written お見合 without its okurigana. The standard spelling is お見合い (reading おみあい), so learners may copy the incomplete form.
issues.suggestion: Write it as お見合(みあ)い (お見合い).

issues.concern: 切り取る means to cut out or cut away a part and remove it. It does not imply keeping the piece for later use; for example, 腫瘍を切り取る means to cut out a tumour. The 'for later use' restriction is overstated.
issues.suggestion: - 切(き)り取(と)る: to cut out — emphasizes cutting away and removing a portion (e.g., a coupon, an article, a tumor)

issues.concern: The notes say that in sense 2 たらたら always follows the noun directly. The entry's own examples contradict this: examples 4 and 5 use 言い訳をたらたらと並べた and 愚痴をたらたらこぼす, where たらたら is an adverb modifying a following verb. Direct attachment (文句たらたら) is one common pattern, not the only one.
issues.suggestion: Say that たらたら often follows the noun directly (文句たらたら, 愚痴たらたら), and can also modify a verb, as in 愚痴をたらたらこぼす.

issues.concern: パンプス is not limited to low or medium heels. The term covers strapless slip-on court shoes of any heel height, including high and stiletto heels. Example 2 itself uses 細いヒールのパンプス.
issues.suggestion: パンプス: pumps — strapless slip-on court shoes, usually with a heel (of any height)

issues.concern: There is no clear evidence that the ticking sense is the original meaning of コチコチ. Standard dictionaries list the 'hard/stiff' senses first, so this etymological claim appears unsupported.
issues.suggestion: Delete the claim, or reword it neutrally: 'Sense 2 (ticking) is a sound-imitating use.'

issues.concern: The '(food-only)' restriction on くちゃくちゃ is false. Besides noisy chewing (including gum), くちゃくちゃ commonly means crumpled or wrinkled (くちゃくちゃの紙) and messy or disordered.
issues.suggestion: Drop '(food-only)', or write: 'くちゃくちゃ: chewing noisily with the mouth open (also means crumpled/wrinkled)'

issues.concern: Nara Prefecture is normally described as Wakayama's neighbor to the east (or northeast). Osaka Prefecture is the neighbor to the north.
issues.suggestion: Change to 'neighbor to the east/northeast' and optionally add 大阪府(おおさかふ) as the northern neighbor.

issues.concern: お元気ですか uses the polite です form and is common in letters and polite speech, so calling it casual is wrong. The casual form would be 元気？
issues.suggestion: Reword as: 'お元気ですか: are you well? — the everyday polite way to ask directly (casual: 元気？)'

issues.concern: The explanation says 築 is 'almost exclusively' seen in real estate listings. That restriction is false: 築〜年 is common in everyday conversation, news and articles about buildings. The entry's own notes also say it appears in casual descriptions.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 'Common in real estate listings, but also used in everyday talk about a building's age.'

issues.concern: The etymology is wrong. ちく is the Sino-Japanese on'yomi of the kanji 築, borrowed from Chinese. It is not derived from the native verb 築く (きずく); both are simply readings of the same kanji.
issues.suggestion: Say: 'This is the on'yomi ちく of the kanji 築, which is also used to write the native verb 築(きず)く (to build).'

issues.concern: The literal meaning given for 築浅 is wrong. 浅 means 'shallow', so it literally means 'shallow (few) years since construction', not 'newly built'.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 'recently built (literally "shallow in building age")'.

issues.concern: 紛争危険地帯 is not a common collocation. The standard term for 'conflict zone' is 紛争地帯, so this listing may mislead learners into using a rare or unnatural compound.
issues.suggestion: Replace with a genuine collocation (e.g. 危険地帯に住む), or note that 'conflict zone' is normally 紛争地帯.

issues.concern: The explanation says 送信先 is the label of the To: field on forms and email clients. Major Japanese email clients such as Gmail and Outlook label that field 宛先. 送信先 may appear on fax machines or some forms, but it is not the standard To: label.
issues.suggestion: Change to something like: 'Can refer to the address in the To: field; email clients usually label that field 宛先(あてさき).'

issues.concern: 背丈 means height or stature (how tall someone is). It does not emphasize overall build; that is 体格(たいかく).
issues.suggestion: Change to: "- 背丈(せたけ): height, stature — slightly more written; often used as a measure of height (e.g., 背丈ほどの草)"

issues.concern: フライドポテト is generally treated as wasei-eigo, a Japanese coinage from English words. English does not use 'fried potato' as the standard term for fries, so calling it a plain loanword from English is misleading.
issues.suggestion: Say it is wasei-eigo (Japanese-made English) built from 'fried' + 'potato'; the English equivalents are 'French fries' (US) or 'chips' (UK).

issues.concern: しゅんとする is colloquial and mimetic (from the onomatopoeic しゅん), not literary. Calling it 'slightly more literary' gives it the wrong register.
issues.suggestion: Describe it as colloquial, e.g. 'similar; mimetic, often used for a sudden subdued silence after being scolded'.

issues.concern: The claim that 無認可 is used 'almost exclusively' to modify nouns is false. It is also commonly used adverbially with で (無認可で営業する) and as a predicate with だ (無認可だ), and the entry's own collocations and example 2 show both.
issues.suggestion: Say it is most often used to modify nouns (directly or with の), but also appears as 無認可で (adverbial) and 無認可だ (predicate).

issues.concern: Calling 無許可 'often for informal permission' is misleading. 無許可 is very commonly used for official or legal permits (無許可営業, 無許可デモ, 無許可建築) and is not mainly about informal permission.
issues.suggestion: 無許可(むきょか): without permission/a permit (broader; covers both official permits and everyday permission)

issues.concern: シュークリームパイ is not an established compound. 'Cream puff pastry' means choux pastry, which is a different dough from パイ生地, so the line misleads learners.
issues.suggestion: Remove this line or replace it with a standard compound such as パンプキンパイ — pumpkin pie.

issues.concern: The translation adds 'making'. 手軽にパイ料理が楽しめる means 'you can easily enjoy pie dishes', not specifically the act of making them.
issues.suggestion: Using frozen puff pastry sheets, you can easily enjoy pie dishes.

issues.concern: 飲み会 means drinking parties in general, not specifically work parties, so the translation adds a workplace setting that the Japanese does not state.
issues.suggestion: Young people these days are sensitive to alcohol harassment at drinking parties and tend to dislike being forced to attend.

issues.concern: 苛立たしい is not limited to the source of irritation. It routinely describes the speaker's own feeling of irritation and impatience, as in 苛立たしい思い and 苛立たしい気持ち. The notes' own collocation 苛立たしい思いをする ('to feel irritated') contradicts this claim.
issues.suggestion: Describes both the feeling of irritation or impatience and the thing that provokes it.

issues.concern: 苛立たしくなる normally means the experiencer starts to feel irritated or frustrated, not that something becomes irritating.
issues.suggestion: 苛立たしくなる: to grow irritated / start to feel frustrated

issues.concern: 崩れ落ちる is very commonly used of people collapsing, as in 膝から崩れ落ちる and その場に崩れ落ちる. The claim that it is 'not people' is a false restriction.
issues.suggestion: Say it is used of structures and also of people who crumple or sink to the ground, for example from shock or grief.

issues.concern: The explanation claims 鉄拳 is used figuratively for authoritarian control. That looks like a calque of the English 'iron fist'. Japanese dictionaries give only the literal sense: a clenched fist, or a blow with one (as in 鉄拳制裁).
issues.suggestion: Remove the figurative 'authoritarian control' sense from the explanation, or mark it as rare and influenced by English.

issues.concern: '鉄拳で治める' is not an established Japanese collocation. 'Rule with an iron fist' is normally expressed with phrases like 強権で治める or 鉄の拳で.
issues.suggestion: Delete this collocation, or replace it with an attested one such as 鉄拳を見舞う or 鉄拳を食らわせる.

issues.concern: The claim of figurative use for 'harsh, domineering control' is not well supported in Japanese, where the word is essentially literal.
issues.suggestion: Say instead that it is used mainly literally, especially in 鉄拳制裁.

issues.concern: The Japanese example relies on a figurative use of 鉄拳 that is not idiomatic. A learner would pick up an unnatural calque.
issues.suggestion: Replace the example with a literal one, e.g. 彼は相手に鉄拳を見舞った。 'He landed a hard punch on his opponent.'

issues.concern: The notes call the word formal, but the formality tag is 'neutral'. 悪事 is common in everyday speech and news (e.g. 悪事を働く), so 'formal, slightly literary' overstates its register. Either the note or the tag is inconsistent.
issues.suggestion: Keep formality 'neutral' and soften the note to e.g. 'A somewhat written-leaning term for immoral or criminal acts; 悪いこと is the everyday equivalent.'

issues.concern: False claim: the 50-yen coin also has a hole in the center, so the five-yen coin is not the only holed Japanese coin.
issues.suggestion: Say it is one of two Japanese coins with a center hole (with the 50-yen coin), and the only brass one with a hole.

issues.concern: 'Kept saying the truth' is unidiomatic English. The natural collocation is 'tell the truth', and 'say the truth' is a common learner error this example would reinforce.
issues.suggestion: Even though no one believed him, he kept telling the truth.

issues.concern: 一街区 is normally read いちがいく; the native-prefix reading ひとがいく is unusual for this Sino-Japanese compound and may mislead learners.
issues.suggestion: Change the reading to 一街区(いちがいく).

issues.concern: The Japanese has no subject, which by default suggests the speaker did the listening (e.g. a doctor speaking). The translation adds 'the doctor' as agent and 'me/my' as patient, information not present in the Japanese.
issues.suggestion: I placed the stethoscope and listened to the heart sounds.

issues.concern: The English adds 'cursive form', which the Japanese does not say. The Japanese only says the shape of the character for 'joy' looks like 七十七.
issues.suggestion: The term kiju comes from the fact that the character for "joy" looks like the characters for seventy-seven.

issues.concern: つぶる simply means to close or shut the eyes. It does not inherently mean squeezing them tightly shut; that nuance needs ぎゅっと. The entry's own example 2 (closing the eyes calmly while listening to music) contradicts this claim.
issues.suggestion: Change to: "つぶる: specific to closing the eyes (目をつぶる); more colloquial than 閉じる".

issues.concern: Overly restrictive. 倦怠期 is typically used of couples, but it also extends to other relationships (friends) and to things like work or hobbies, where one has grown tired of them.
issues.suggestion: Say the compound is most commonly used of romantic relationships and marriage, and can also describe a phase of weariness with other relationships or activities.

issues.concern: 鶯色 is traditionally a dull, brownish olive green (緑に茶と黒のまじった色), not yellow-green. 'Yellow-green' describes the popular confusion with the メジロ (white-eye) colour.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 鶯(うぐいす)色(いろ): bush warbler color (dull olive green / greenish brown)

issues.concern: 湯がちゃぷちゃぷと揺れて describes the water gently sloshing or lapping. 'Swirled' suggests a circular motion that the Japanese does not express.
issues.suggestion: When I got into the hot spring, the water gently lapped and sloshed around me every time I moved, and it felt wonderful.

issues.concern: のしのし describes a slow, heavy, lumbering or ponderous walk, like an elephant or a sumo wrestler. 'Waddling' suggests a side-to-side, duck-like gait, which is closer to よちよち or よたよた.
issues.suggestion: - のしのし: slow, heavy, lumbering walk

issues.concern: The explanation's claim 'Traditionally lasting 49 days in Buddhism.' confuses 喪 with 忌中(きちゅう). The 49-day period is 忌中, while 喪中 for a close relative traditionally lasts about one year. This is why 喪中はがき covers deaths within the past year.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 'Traditionally lasting about one year for a close relative; the first 49 days (忌中) are the strictest period in Buddhist practice.'

issues.concern: ぱちぱち is used for blinking (目をぱちぱち), not flapping; flapping is バタバタ/パタパタ. The claim misdescribes the contrast word.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'flapping' with 'blinking': '(small fire, applause, blinking)'.

issues.concern: The note restricts イルミネーション too narrowly. The word is not limited to large LED installations in public spaces. It also covers decorative lights on homes, shop fronts and trees, and older non-LED displays such as incandescent bulbs.
issues.suggestion: Say it commonly refers to decorative light displays, often large LED installations at public spaces and attractions, rather than 'specifically'.

issues.concern: In win-loss records, 一分 is written 一分け and read いちわけ ('one draw'). いっぷん means 'one minute', so the reading given is wrong.
issues.suggestion: Change to: 一勝(いっしょう)一分(いちわ)け: one win, one draw

issues.concern: 三十三回忌 is held in the 33rd year after death, counting the year of death as year 1. That is 32 years after death, so it marks the 32nd death anniversary. 'Thirty-third death anniversary' would lead learners to think the service falls 33 years after death. The explanation repeats the problem by calling it 'the 33rd anniversary of a person's death', and its parenthetical does not resolve the contradiction.
issues.suggestion: Gloss as '32nd anniversary of a death; 33rd-year memorial service' and reword the explanation: 'held in the 33rd year after death (32 years after, counting the year of death as the first year)'.

issues.concern: The explanation says these devices measure 'bone density'. Typical body composition scales give an estimated bone mass (推定骨量), not bone density, which needs medical equipment such as DEXA.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'bone density' with 'estimated bone mass' in the explanation.

issues.concern: In Japanese, ストッキング is commonly used as a general term that includes waist-high pantyhose; it is often used interchangeably with パンティストッキング. Saying it means leg-only hosiery with no waist coverage is false for Japanese usage.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite as: 'ストッキング: stockings; in everyday Japanese often used broadly for sheer hosiery, including pantyhose. Thigh-high types are specified as e.g. ガーターストッキング.'

issues.concern: Japanese references usually classify パンティストッキング as wasei-eigo, a Japanese coinage from 'panty' + 'stocking'. The usual English term is 'pantyhose', so 'From English "panty stockings"' is likely a misleading etymology.
issues.suggestion: Change to 'Japanese coinage (wasei-eigo) from English "panty" + "stocking"; the English equivalent is "pantyhose".'

issues.concern: 利口 is listed under the 'sense 1 — profit/benefit' compounds, but in 利口 the kanji 利 means 'sharp/keen' (as in 鋭利), not 'profit/benefit'. This misrepresents how the compound is built.
issues.suggestion: Remove 利口 from the profit/benefit list, or note that here 利 means 'sharp; keen'.

issues.concern: Overstates the restriction. Besides 力ずくで, the attributive 力ずくの + noun is also common, as in 力ずくの解決 and 力ずくのやり方.
issues.suggestion: Say it is most often used as 力ずくで, and also appears as 力ずくの + noun (e.g. 力ずくの解決).

issues.concern: This line calls ようだ the 'colloquial equivalent', but ようだ is the formal/written form. みたいだ is the colloquial one. The line also contradicts itself ('colloquial... more formal/written').
issues.suggestion: - ようだ: formal/written equivalent of みたいだ

issues.concern: そやな does not seek stronger agreement than そやね. In Kansai speech, な is a blunter, more casual (often masculine-sounding) counterpart of ね, and is often more self-directed or assertive. It does not ask the listener for more agreement.
issues.suggestion: Describe そやな as a blunter or more casual variant (often more masculine-sounding), e.g. 'そやな (blunter, more casual variant)'.

issues.concern: The explanation presents 懲役 as current Japanese law, but the revised Penal Code merged 懲役 and 禁錮 into 拘禁刑 from June 1, 2025. The statutory range is also 1 month to 20 years; 30 years is the ceiling only with aggravation.
issues.suggestion: Say that under the Penal Code before June 2025 the range was 1 month to 20 years (up to 30 with aggravation), and that 懲役 has since been replaced by 拘禁刑(こうきんけい).

issues.concern: 生理用品 is not an abbreviated form of 生理用ナプキン. It is a separate, broader term for menstrual or sanitary products, and it covers tampons as well as pads. The usual shortening of 生理用ナプキン is simply ナプキン.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite as: 'In everyday speech it is often shortened to ナプキン. The broader term 生理用品(せいりようひん) refers to menstrual products generally.'

issues.concern: The note glosses 店 with its standalone kun reading みせ. In this compound it is read てん (on reading), so a learner may misread the word.
issues.suggestion: Write 店(てん) (shop, establishment), or note that 店 is read てん here.

issues.concern: 湯炊き means cooking rice by putting it into water that is already boiling, then letting it absorb the measured water. The boil-and-drain method is 湯取り法(ゆとりほう).
issues.suggestion: cooking rice by adding it to already-boiling water

issues.concern: Describes boil-and-drain (湯取り法), not 湯炊き. The explanation repeats the error: in 湯炊き the rice still absorbs a set amount of water and is not drained.
issues.suggestion: method of cooking rice by adding it to already-boiling water (no draining)

issues.concern: Renders 湯炊き as 'boil-and-drain method', which is a different technique.
issues.suggestion: I ate rice that had been cooked by adding it to already-boiling water.

issues.concern: Renders 湯炊き as 'boil-and-drain method', which is 湯取り法.
issues.suggestion: Yudaki, adding rice to already-boiling water, is a traditional way to cook rice without a rice cooker.

issues.concern: The example itself describes boiling in excess water and draining, which is 湯取り法, not 湯炊き. Both the Japanese and the English teach the wrong meaning.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite, e.g. 湯炊きの場合、沸騰したお湯にお米を入れて炊きます。 / 'With yudaki, you put the rice into water that is already boiling.'
